entries.words: A player decides from a screen of moving objects and spaces. To fly like them, and not only as well as them, the AI has to learn from some version of what they saw.
entries.rule: An AI meant to fly like a person learns from what that pilot could see at the moment of each decision, not from the whole world state.
entries.test: Are the AI's training features computed from the pilot's view, not the full world? If from the world, it can play as well as a person but not like one.

entries.words: take the average of the datas and understand how the path can be navigated. Sometimes even I make mistakes, hit things, so you have to ignore those datas. ... a very dynamic AI that feels like playing with another human being.
entries.rule: The AI is learned from people's recorded flights with their mistakes filtered out, toward a dynamic AI that feels like playing with another human being; nothing is labelled by hand.
entries.test: Does the AI design learn from people's play (mistakes excluded) and aim to feel human, rather than a scripted line?

entries.words: every vessel moves in different ways ... they should process in their own way. The ultimate goal is to win the race fast ... how risky you want to play versus how careful
entries.rule: Each hull's racing AI is its own set of skills matching how that vessel moves, each learned and measured on its own, then raced together; there is no one generic racer.
entries.test: Does the AI design give every hull the same brain, or one tuned to that hull's own verbs and risk?

entries.words: the charge arena game ... that is like a dogfight rumble where players attack each other
entries.rule: Combat balance is found by optimising each hull's AI in mirror matches in its Charge arcade game until its petal score plateaus, then against the other hulls in Broadside, then adjusting each hull's effects until every plateau is the same; nothing is balanced against an AI that has not plateaued.
entries.test: Does the balance change rest on plateaued AIs scored on petals taken, in mirror matches first and Broadside second? If it is tuned by feel, it is off the plan.

entries.words: AI learning is automatic (LOCKED rule, Yash, 2026-10-26) ... "I don't wanna click any commands or anything. Never."
entries.rule: The AIs learn from recorded human play on their own: every editor race is recorded and sent automatically and the learning sweep relearns the AIs from it; no person is ever asked to run a learner, report or test command.
entries.test: Does any step of the AI design ask a person to click or run something? If so it fails; the learner joins the automatic sweep instead.

entries.words: I don't wanna click any commands or anything. Never. This is a rule. ... every time I'm playing a new game, the record should just come here and then you evaluate what type of data the new game has ... and then relearn its AI navigation in order to win the race.
entries.rule: Every race a person plays is recorded and learned from on its own; no person is ever asked to run a learner, report or test command for the AI to improve.
entries.test: Does the design ask a person to run anything for the AI to learn from their play? If yes it breaks the rule.

entries.words: The sparrow can use its shooting ability to clear up space in front of you for it to race down the track. This way we have to train the sparrow AIs. And also other AIs should be able to use their ability in order to gain advantage on racing, in their own minigame races.
entries.rule: A racing AI uses its hull's own abilities to win its race (the Sparrow's rocket and guns, the Dolphin's drift and charge, the Stoat's sling), one drive per hull per minigame learned from people's races; a blind ability timer is not an AI.
entries.test: Does the AI for a mode fire the hull's abilities as racing decisions, or only on a timer? A timer-only AI is unfinished.

entries.words: While playing any racing game mode, AI should not go for crystals. It should only focus on waypoints. If the crystals are the waypoints, then go for crystals.
entries.rule: In a race an AI flies the waypoints and never detours for a crystal, unless the crystals are the waypoints.
entries.retired: the 200-220 u crystal detour slack (aiCrystalDetourSlack) in every gate race
entries.test: Does a racing AI leave its line for a crystal that is not a waypoint? If yes it is wrong.

entries.words: The host picks the AI difficulty - Easy, Medium, Hard or Legendary - on every card (AIDifficultyRules.IsOfferedFor, Yash 2026-10-26: "a generic rule"
entries.rule: Every card offers the host one AI difficulty row (Easy / Medium / Hard / Legendary) and every AI reads it through one handicap of its own.
entries.test: Does the new mode or AI take the lobby difficulty through one handicap, with the row offered on its card?

entries.words: The AIs train in each vessel's OWN minigames (its Time minigame first), never in Regatta; the arena games are rebuilt later from those skills
entries.rule: An AI is trained in its own vessel's minigames (Time first), never in Regatta or any arena; arena play is rebuilt later from those skills.
entries.test: Name the minigame the AI trains in; a Regatta or arena training run fails.

entries.words: We are not using the regatta scene to train the AIs, rather we are using the AIs own mini-games, time mini-games, to train them. [...] we will pick each vessel, we will keep playing their own time mini-games, whether racing or other time mini-games.
entries.rule: An AI trains in its own vessel's minigames, its Time minigame first, never in Regatta or any arena game; the arena games are rebuilt later from the skills learned there.
entries.retired: Regatta as the AI training ground (the learning sweep reports Regatta races and learns nothing from them)
entries.test: Does the AI work learn from or tune in an arena game? If yes it is out; the vessel's own Time game is where it learns.

entries.words: Each AI can also carry its own level (Shombith and Yash, 2026-10-27): on every card with the AI row, Arcade and Arena, the host presses an AI's podium and the row then sets that AI only; with no AI selected it sets every AI.
entries.rule: On every card with the AI row the host may set one AI's level by selecting its podium, or every AI's with none selected; each level reaches that AI as it spawns.
entries.test: Can the host set a single AI seat's level on the card, and does it reach that seat alone?

entries.words: Every flight says who flew it; the AI never learns from the AI
entries.rule: Every recorded flight names its pilot (human, mixed, AI or trainer) and only a person's flights reach a learner; the AI never learns from a flight the AI or the trainer flew.
entries.test: Could a machine-flown match enter the learning data as a person's? If yes the pilot field or the not-a-person gate is missing.

entries.words: AI training serves one plan (LOCKED rule, Garrett, 2026-11-02) ... one universal AI per vessel per element, trained on that element's arcade game and scored on I1-I4 together ... No AI is trained inside an arena game.
entries.rule: Every AI effort serves the one AI plan: one universal AI per vessel per element, trained on that element's arcade game and scored on I1-I4 together, with the pilot only biasing its choices; the ladder is arcade intensities, then the arena balanced against those fixed AIs, then voyages; no AI is trained inside an arena game.
entries.test: Name the ai_plan.json step the work serves and check the AI is per vessel per element, trained in that element's arcade game; a per-mode or arena-trained AI fails.

entries.words: We need our planning and learning to be working towards an AI training system that produces all the AI capabilities we need. The culminating experience is voyages. The AI you are playing against or with will be determined by the choices during squad configuration: vessel, element, pilot, artifact.
entries.rule: Every AI effort serves one plan: one universal AI per vessel per element, trained in that element's arcade game over I1-I4, then the element's arena balanced against those fixed AIs, then voyages, where the squad seat's cards (vessel, element, pilot) choose the AI.
entries.retired: the three drive searches trained inside Regatta and the two one-intensity Squirrel searches (ai_plan.json retired_jobs)
entries.test: Does the AI work name the plan step it serves (ai_plan.json), train in the element's arcade game and not in an arena, and produce one genome scored over all four intensities?

entries.words: A pilot never changes what the vessel can do. A game mode never changes the vessel (CLAUDE.md, LOCKED), and neither does a pilot. A pilot only changes what the AI goes after.
entries.rule: A pilot card changes only what its AI goes after (a bias on targets toward what the callsign sees); it never changes what the vessel can do, and neither does a mode.
entries.test: Does the pilot or mode design alter a vessel's abilities, numbers or kit? If yes it is a vessel change for the vessel's owner, not a pilot or mode feature.

entries.words: One genome per vessel per element. The deliverable of an arcade step is ONE AI per vessel for that element, scored on a composite over all four intensities of that element's arcade game(s)
entries.rule: The deliverable AI for a vessel and element is one universal genome scored on all four intensities together (the mean plus half the worst); per-intensity and per-mode files are seeds and data, never the deliverable.
entries.retired: the two one-intensity Squirrel searches
entries.test: Does the AI work produce or promote a per-intensity or per-mode file as the answer? If yes it is a seed, not the deliverable.

entries.words: The arena is searched against fixed AIs; no AI is trained inside it.
entries.rule: An arena game (Regatta, Broadside, ...) is balanced (course, features, elemental baselines) with every vessel's promoted universal genome held fixed; no AI is ever trained inside an arena game, and nothing is balanced against an AI that has not converged.
entries.test: Does the design train, tune or learn an AI inside an arena game, or balance an arena against a still-moving AI? Either is out.

entries.words: Balance in this order: the arena to the vessels, then the vessels to their elements (each vessel's elemental baseline).
entries.rule: Balance the arena to the trained vessels first (its course and features), and only then the vessels to their elements through the smallest elemental baseline change.
entries.test: Does a balance change touch a vessel's elemental baseline before the arena's course and features were searched? If yes it is out of order.

entries.words: Thresher's time game need to be made first before regatta, thats the rule, make AIs good in their vessel's respective time game, then we will design regatta based on those AI skills and game modes.
entries.rule: A vessel joins an arena card (Regatta) only after its AI is good in its own Time game at I1-I4; the arena is designed from those AI skills, never the other way round.
entries.test: Does the design seat a vessel in an arena game before its Time-game AI finishes all four intensities? If yes it is early.

entries.words: input-only - an AI reads what a pilot can see and writes only the vessel's input channels
entries.rule: An AI reads only what a pilot can see and writes only the vessel's input channels; it never writes vessel or world state.
entries.test: Does the AI design read hidden state or write anything but input? It fails (check_ai_no_state_writes.py).

entries.words: A pursuing AI ORBITS anything inside its own minimum turn radius, and that is geometry rather than tuning
entries.rule: An AI that cannot reach a target inside its turning circle extends and re-attacks (fly out, come around, come back); the radius derives from live speed, never an authored constant, and turning harder is the wrong fix.
entries.test: Does the pursuit design break an orbit by extending rather than by tuning turn rate, with the capture radius included?

entries.words: Audio (FMOD) — every sound is an exposed, editable field (LOCKED convention) ... Every noise anything makes must be an inspector-exposed EventReference on the prefab/component (or SO) that makes it.
entries.rule: Every sound is an inspector-exposed EventReference on the thing that makes it, one field per ability per distinct sound; a slot with no sound ships empty and silent, never a borrowed temp event, and only genuinely platform-wide sounds use a shared category.
entries.test: For each sound the design makes, name the component field that holds it; a hardcoded event path, a temp event or a new ability on a shared category fails.

entries.words: render the shrimp view as true to the game as possible; err on the side of being too true to the game.
entries.rule: A seat's special view (the Pistol's side view) is the real game drawn by the real renderer with real meshes and materials, never a stylised stand-in.
entries.test: Is the view a real camera on the real scene with the real materials? A drawn or simplified copy errs the wrong way.

entries.words: "the prisms that go out of plane for the kite should be unlit but not disappear"
entries.rule: The Kite's view draws out-of-plane prisms as unlit ghost boxes by Garrett's call; ask before applying the no-flat rule to someone else's deliberate look.
entries.test: Before "fixing" a flat or unlit look, check whether an owner asked for exactly that and where it is recorded.

entries.words: the sniper should keep the Serpent's pip scope open instead of zooming the whole camera
entries.rule: A scope is a picture-in-picture, never a zoom of the whole gameplay camera.
entries.test: Does an aiming ability change the main camera's field of view beyond the one sanctioned fixed scope zoom? If yes, make it a pip.

entries.words: "make sure anyone else using orthographic view never applies a panini or bloom to 2d assets by default."
entries.rule: An orthographic (2D) camera never gets Panini (nothing can opt in), and its 2D marks (icons, dots, rings, cords, petals) skip post-processing through an overlay while the world under them keeps bloom.
entries.test: Does the 2D view register with OrthographicLens and draw its marks through an UnprocessedOverlay (check_orthographic_views.py)?

entries.words: I want the camera to be a little bit alive rather than just ... the vessel staying fixed in the centre of the screen no matter what.
entries.rule: The gameplay camera is a little alive: skims wiggle it, hits land with an impact shake, drifts and shots are felt, with inertia that differs by hull (a heavier hull's pilot feels less, an agile one's more), all subtle and never fancy.
entries.test: Does the camera react to skims, hits, shots and acceleration, scaled by hull, while staying subtle (not too much, not too fancy) and under the player's shake setting?

entries.words: "the characters with an orthographic view like the shrimp are doing something weird with the voroni effect on the skybox"; "call these 2d cameras"
entries.rule: A 2D camera (one that slides and zooms across a plane) fades the sky's Voronoi cell net; stars, nebulae and the galactic band stay; every new 2D camera registers itself.
entries.test: Is the new 2D camera registered with TwoDCameraSky so the cell net fades through its lens?

entries.words: these sort of features are disruptive to the players sense of their reference frame, position, speed, etc. Our game is truly 3d and usually does its best to not have an 'up' ... we do things to help players, but we can't do things like drift displacement that hinder them.
entries.rule: A drift, or any camera-feel effect, never displaces the hull on screen: the camera may rumble or tilt a few degrees, but the hull keeps its screen position so the pilot's read of reference frame, position and speed is never hindered.
entries.retired: the camera's drift slide (driftSlide, driftSlideIn, driftSlideOut; built 2026-10-25, removed 2026-11-02)
entries.test: Does any camera behaviour move the hull's screen position or heading read in a way the pilot did not command? If yes, it hinders the pilot: drop it.

entries.words: Speed is a property of every vessel, so the visual language for speed belongs to every vessel.
entries.rule: The speed tunnel (FOV narrowing with Panini relaxing as measured speed rises) is one absolute fleet-wide law: the same speed gives the same visual on every vessel; no vessel or mode may author it off, scale it or normalise it to its own top speed.
entries.test: Does the design add a per-vessel or per-mode speed visual, window, scalar or opt-out? If yes it breaks the platform law.

entries.words: Prisms between the player's camera and their ship go see-through so the ship is never hidden — not a feature a vessel or mode may choose; it must not be possible to author one in which it is off
entries.rule: Prisms between the player's camera and their ship always go see-through; no vessel, mode or scene can switch the corridor off.
entries.retired: the per-vessel opt-in ClearPrisms
entries.test: Can the ship be hidden behind prisms in any view the design adds, or does any prism material lack the corridor fade?

entries.words: Every vessel's gameplay camera narrows its FOV below home while the URP Panini distance drops below the profile baseline, both proportional to that vessel's LIVE speed — a quasi dolly zoom with no camera-distance change. Not a feature a vessel or mode may choose.
entries.rule: Every gameplay camera runs the speed tunnel off live speed with one absolute mapping (the same speed looks the same on any vessel); never a per-vessel window, scalar or normalisation to its own top speed.
entries.retired: a per-vessel speed window / normalise-to-own-top-speed (considered and rejected)
entries.test: Does the design give a vessel its own tunnel scale or FOV write? It fails; move the tunnel's home, never Camera.fieldOfView.

entries.words: One authorized exception (the designer, 2026-10-16): the Angler's KEEPER. The first creature in an Angler's school does not starve, and an Angler with an empty school has one born to it.
entries.rule: Only the first creature of an Angler's school is kept from starving (predation, jousts and lost body prisms still kill it); it is an exception, never a precedent.
entries.test: A design waiving starvation for anything but the keeper (one reader, one implementer) needs its own sign-off.

entries.words: when spindles wither or die lets have them instead morph into a new shard that gets added to the shard list.
entries.rule: A dying limb condenses into a cytoplasm shard on its own fade clock (one limb in five; the rest evaporate), so nothing pops and no shard is ever removed to make room.
entries.test: Does a limb's death end in nothing, pop, or evict an existing shard? Each breaks continuity.

entries.words: "a special swarm that can be upgraded to break rules and should only starve down to a minimum size"
entries.rule: The Jacks' herd starves only down to its minimum size and an empty herd has that many born to it; every other rule a herd may break is an explicit IFaunaHerd method with one reader.
entries.test: Does a herd rule-break go through IFaunaHerd with one reader in Fauna, and does it waive only starvation down to the floor?

entries.words: "in general shielded prisms should be food during a frenzy when the cell has too many prism"
entries.rule: A cell in Frenzy has too much mass, so its fauna may eat shielded mass too; outside a Frenzy a shielded prism is off the menu.
entries.test: Is shielded mass edible only while the cell is in Frenzy?

entries.words: its spindles lean a little toward its tamer's domain hue so a player can tell their herd or school from the wild (Garrett, 2026-10-21, IFaunaLeash.TryGetLeashMark), while its domain, body prisms and diet stay the cell's.
entries.rule: A tamed creature shows its tamer only by a slight hue lean of its spindles; its domain, body prisms and diet stay the cell's.
entries.test: Does taming change anything but the spindle hue lean? Then it fails.

entries.words: A DYING LIMB BECOMES A CYTOPLASM SHARD (Garrett, 2026-10-21). Every spindle that withers or dies may leave a new shard in its cell's SnowChanger field
entries.rule: A withering spindle may condense into a cytoplasm shard on its own fade clock (every fifth limb, after Garrett toned it down 5x the same day); shards carry no mass and no collider, and a shard is never culled to make room.
entries.test: Do shards keep the ordered wither ordered, carry no mass, and never get culled?

entries.words: "if an opposing team's fauna is netted it steals it" and "lets have the omnicrystal produce an omnivorous worm fauna in the player's domain"
entries.rule: A creature changes domain only through the Jacks' net steal, and is born in a player's colour only through the Jacks' omni crystal; its offspring inherit that colour and nothing else about it changes (it eats, breeds, starves and dies by its own rules).
entries.test: Does any other ability recolour or birth a creature in a player's domain? Then it needs its own sign-off.

entries.words: Change the scale of the fauna to match the size of crystal. You will also need to crawl swarm behavior etc. for length scales and adjust accordingly.
entries.rule: Every creature is scaled to the one crystal size keeping its designed heart:body proportion; body-measured lengths (spacing, reach, bite) scale with it, speeds stay in world units.
entries.test: Does a new creature's heart fit the one crystal size, and do its lengths derive from its body while its speeds stay absolute?

entries.words: The sharks have a mass crystal that would be fine, but with the effect on mass crystals where the triangular segments socket in and out of the crystal, the segments end up clipping with the shark's spindle body ... let mass have size.
entries.rule: A Mass creature has size: its body holds the Mass heart's full segment swing clear of every shield, so the crystal's columns never clip the body.
entries.test: Does the Mass form keep the heart's swing clear of its own shields? If not, grow or reshape the body, never shrink the crystal.

entries.words: the space spindle needs to be universally scaled to bigger than mass, but we must erode and thin its thickest sections so the whole spindle gets more spindly
entries.rule: A Space creature is scaled whole beyond its Mass sibling (by the lattice's own Space:Mass reach) and eroded thinner where it is thickest, so Space takes room: more spread, more reach, a spindlier body.
entries.test: Is the Space form longer than the Mass form and thinner at its thickest, with spacing and reach 1.35x? If it is merely bigger, it is Mass again.

entries.words: you stretched it such that the crystal inside is also getting stretched, always be careful about stretching hierarchically
entries.rule: An elemental form reshapes only a creature's own body skins; the heart crystal is never stretched, eroded or scaled with the body.
entries.test: After the element's reshaping, is the heart crystal still the one size and shape? If it moved with the body, the hierarchy stretched it.

entries.words: We are going to loose the 'chunky' prisms now that we have these scaled up versions of mass. Lets also shift the shielding affect from charge to mass ... Then the new charge affect will be to make all of its prisms danger prism, not just the select ones the other elements have.
entries.rule: Mass is the armoured element (its shield carries its volume, hearts seated clear), Charge makes every prism of its lifeform a danger prism, and no element has chunky prisms.
entries.retired: the chunky Mass prisms; Charge as the shielding element
entries.test: Does a lifeform's Mass form carry the shield and its Charge form make all its prisms danger? Any other mapping breaks the fleet law.

entries.words: no space should always have greater span but significantly less volume, more spindly, and thinner where it is thickest. the shielding should increase the volume of mass
entries.rule: Space always out-spans Mass with significantly less volume (spindlier, thinner at its thickest), and Mass's shielding is what adds volume; a Mass form never out-spans its Space sibling.
entries.test: Measure span and volume of the Space and Mass forms: Space wider, Mass heavier. If Mass spans further, it is wrong.

entries.words: the wall flora can retire so the serpent wall feels less synthetic
entries.rule: A vessel's own construction (the Serpent's wall) is never also a plant: the Wall flora is retired so the wall reads as the vessel's, not as ecology.
entries.retired: the Wall flora (prefab, four configs, the Spawn Matrix row, the Codex entry, AssembledFlora.PreviewWall)
entries.test: Does a plant reuse a vessel's own prism as its leaf, or a vessel structure read as a plant? If yes one of them must go.

entries.words: a bunch of the swarm fauna are still using outdated versions of the inactive crystals, etc. lets finish this job. make the elements complete and consistent and polished for all life forms
entries.rule: Every lifeform, the data-driven ones (swarms, builder colonies, substrates) included, expresses all four elements by the one fleet law (heart, armour, danger, span), complete and consistent.
entries.test: Does every element form of the new lifeform exist and follow the fleet law, data-driven bodies included?

entries.words: "the omnicrystal on board the ark powers the prism creation. arks are the only vessel that can contain and harvest the power of an omnicrystal instead of morphing it into something else", "regeneration should just be fixed rate", and "the omnicrystal is always just one size"
entries.rule: Mass may be made in one place only: an Ark's reactor regrows the Ark's own empty hull slots, one prism a beat at a fixed rate, never past its full hull; every other vessel morphs an omni crystal into its own effect; the omni crystal is always one size; a fallen Ark never regrows.
entries.test: Does anything but the Ark's reactor create mass, does the rate vary, or does anything resize the omni crystal? Each fails.

entries.words: "lets also shift the shielding affect from charge to mass ... then the new charge affect will be to make all of its prisms danger prism, not just the select ones the other elements have"
entries.rule: On plants and creatures alike Mass is armoured (its prisms shielded and re-armoured for life, the shield 3x the prism), Charge makes every prism danger and never shields, every element keeps its authored danger, and Space always out-spans Mass (greater span, less volume, more spindly).
entries.retired: CHARGE armours its mass (the rule until 2026-10-28); the "chunky" Mass plate
entries.test: Does the lifeform's Mass form shield, its Charge form arm every prism, and its Space form out-span Mass?

entries.words: the mutualistic and productive nature of bees places them as a fauna that acts more like a flora in terms of their effect on the ecology. thus thery can take the slot of a productive flora instead of a consuming fauna.
entries.rule: A pollinator is a third fauna role beside herbivore and predator: it produces (hastens plants, builds comb), takes a productive flora's slot and budget, and is prey like every non-predator.
entries.test: Does the new creature's ecological role fit herbivore, predator or pollinator, with its budget charged to the right kingdom?

entries.words: A fauna's ROLE is not fixed by its kingdom (Garrett, 2026-10-31, Docs/ECOSYSTEM.md §66): besides the CONSUMERS (FaunaDiet.Herbivore eats prism mass, Predator eats herbivores) there are POLLINATORS (FaunaDiet.Pollinator, the bees), fauna whose effect is PRODUCTIVE.
entries.rule: A fauna may be a consumer (herbivore, predator) or a pollinator whose effect is productive: it eats nothing, hastens flora growth, carries only transferred mass, and its population is raised by its home flora, so it sits on the producer side and never starves.
entries.test: Which role does the creature play, and does a productive one mint nothing (transfer only) and take a flora slot for its home?

entries.words: they should pollinate all three
entries.rule: Pollination is mutualism across all three domains: a bee hastens plants of any domain and builds its comb from all three; it is not a team fight.
entries.test: Does a mutualistic behaviour discriminate by domain? If yes it has become a team mechanic.

entries.words: fauna have rules like bodies made of spindles that are wireframe inspired structures suitable for the space element to make thinner. there must be a long skinny danger prism as a stinger. ... it is a celestial etherion based life form. it doesn't really have a sense of up
entries.rule: A creature is a celestial Etherion lifeform, never an Earth animal: a wireframe spindle body Space can thin, health prisms round it, a long skinny danger prism as its stinger, an Etherion heart that leads, and no sense of up.
entries.test: Does the creature design lean on an Earth body (legs, a ground, an up), lack a stinger or health prisms, or hide its spindles?

entries.words: the stinger can thin on space. the stinger is just a danger prism. danger prisms are left behind without need for exceptions
entries.rule: A creature's danger prism (stinger, tooth, spine) is an ordinary prism: it thins on Space with the rest and stays in the skeleton like every other body prism; no special case.
entries.retired: the 'a tooth keeps its size' exemption from Space erosion
entries.test: Does the design give a danger prism special treatment in erosion, death or the skeleton? If yes, remove the exception.

entries.words: It is still PREY (Garrett, 2026-11-01: predators eat bees; FaunaDiets.IsPrey), it pollinates flora of every domain, and its home is built from all three domains
entries.rule: A pollinator is prey (predators eat bees), pollinates every domain's flora, and its home is built from the mass of whichever domain paid for each cell.
entries.test: Is the pollinator edible to predators and domain-blind in what it pollinates?

entries.words: Invariant — mass is conserved (no passive decay) ... A prism — whether a lifeform's health-prism or vessel-spawned — is only ever removed by an active force
entries.rule: A prism is removed only by an active force (a vessel's ability, or fauna eating it); there is no passive decay, lifespan, timed culler, trail cap or idle removal, and a large accumulation is a valid state the food web resolves (two signed-off exceptions only: the Wanderway tether; the MobileLow Skim Race and Joust trail cap).
entries.test: Does the design remove, cap, age or recycle prisms without an active force consuming them? If yes it needs an owner's signed-off exception in ECOSYSTEM.md section 0.

entries.words: One fauna colour per cell. A tamed creature keeps the cell's colour (LOCKED, `ECOSYSTEM_DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md`). "My squad" is a leash relationship, not a team.
entries.rule: Every creature in a cell wears the cell's one fauna colour; taming or leashing never recolours it, because a squad is a leash, not a team.
entries.test: Does the design recolour a creature for its owner, squad or team? If yes it breaks the one-colour rule.

entries.words: I can imagine being surrounded by them and having them all dive in at once will be scary once the stakes are felt.
entries.rule: The substrate pack's feel is being surrounded and then having them all dive in at once, scary once the stakes are felt.
entries.test: Does the pack's behaviour build a surround and a simultaneous dive the player can feel coming?

entries.words: Cells (with CellType) — the regions of play that are the unit of territorial control. Casual language sometimes calls these "biomes"; the canonical term is cell.
entries.rule: The unit of territorial control is the Cell; territory, phase and population are expressed through it.
entries.test: Does the design express territory and its environment through a Cell rather than a system of its own?

entries.words: Ark — a mothership: a prism-bodied home that travels the hypersea, wears a domain, and lives or dies by the food web.
entries.rule: An Ark's hull is ordinary conserved mass in its domain, attacked and defended purely through the shipped diet rules (protecting an Ark is controlling the cell, no aggro system); it is not a LifeForm (no heart, no starvation clock, no reproduction), dies when its last hull prism is destroyed, and imposes no timer on anything.
entries.test: Does the Ark design add an aggro system, a lifeform heart, a clock or non-prism hull mass? Any of these fails.

entries.words: prisms are conserved; the only sinks are active — vessel abilities and fauna consumption.
entries.rule: A frozen cell is never fixed by prism decay, a reaper or a TTL; give an active force a reason to consume the mass (fauna diet, reach, spawning, abilities) and accept a large uneaten accumulation as a valid equilibrium.
entries.retired: passive prism decay and the per-tick reaper (rejected); the flora regrowth pulse (flagged for retirement, not extension)
entries.test: How does mass leave the cell in this design? Only by abilities or eating; any timer fails.

entries.words: Ecosystem Design Principles (LOCKED — read before any ecology change) ... These invariants are locked — do not relitigate or re-derive them.
entries.rule: The ecosystem invariants (continuity of existence, no imposed death, no domain asymmetry, conserved mass, volume as the spine, one crystal per lifeform, territorial permanence, endogenous selection, the Cell owns the environment) are locked; an ecology, fauna, flora or HyperSea change restates which it touches and violates none.
entries.test: The brief lists the invariants it touches and shows none is violated; a brief that re-derives one fails.

entries.words: No imposed death. No decay, lifespan, or fixed-period despawn timers. Populations are bounded by consumption + starvation, never an imposed clock. (Repeatedly rejected.)
entries.rule: No lifeform has a lifespan, decay or despawn timer; populations are bounded only by consumption and starvation; the fenced exceptions (the Angler's keeper, a herd's floor) waive starvation for one creature or a minimum, never kill.
entries.test: Does any lifeform in the design die or despawn on a clock? It fails.

entries.words: No domain asymmetry. Fauna spawn in one color — the cell's controlling color. Never cross-domain / prey-weighted / per-domain-biased spawning.
entries.rule: Fauna are born in exactly one colour, the cell's controller's, and a cell never holds two fauna colours except through the fenced exceptions (the Jacks' net steal, the Jacks' omni worm, MultiDomain swarm lineages); a mode may redefine what controls a cell but never the one-colour spawn.
entries.test: In what colour is each creature born, and is any spawn weighted by domain or prey? Any second colour must be one of the fenced exceptions.

entries.words: Super-shielded mass is never food, in any cell
entries.rule: Super-shielded mass is never food and never a steering target; shielded mass is food only during a Frenzy or for a herd whose upgrade allows it (the one granted exception: Cell.ArmourIsFood on the Ark escort's own worlds, Garrett 2026-10-31); fauna are never led to mass they cannot eat.
entries.test: Does any grazer in the design eat or chase shielded or super-shielded mass outside a Frenzy, a herd upgrade or ArmourIsFood?

entries.words: THE NAMED EXCEPTION: a MultiDomain SWARM grows regional LINEAGES ... food never colours anyone
entries.rule: Only a sort-model swarm with MultiDomain on may grow a second colour, by lineage drift in tissue nobody owns, never by what it eats; no other species gets lineages.
entries.retired: round 8's diet colouring (tried and removed on playtest)
entries.test: Does anything colour a creature by its food, or extend lineages to a non-swarm species? It fails.

entries.words: A creature dies when its last body prism is destroyed
entries.rule: A creature dies when its last body prism is destroyed, through the one sealed death path (crystal drop and wither included); no override may let a creature survive losing its whole body.
entries.test: Can a creature in the design lose every body prism and live? Then it fails.

entries.words: Starvation = wither-to-crystal, and a joust is that wither RUN BACKWARDS.
entries.rule: A starving creature withers from its extremities inward with the heart last and collectable only at the end; a jousted lifeform unravels from the freed heart outward and the jouster auto-collects it; both leave the body prisms standing as grazeable skeleton; a devoured body suctions into the mouth.
entries.test: Name the death style (Withered / Jousted / Consumed) of every death in the design and check nothing vanishes and the skeleton stays as mass.

entries.words: Every standing spindle and prism of a lifeform always has a path of standing spindles to its crystal
entries.rule: In growth, under grazing and through every death, every standing part of a lifeform connects to its crystal through standing spindles; the crystal joust is the one sanctioned exception.
entries.test: Can any part of the body be left standing with no spindle path to the heart? Only a joust may.

entries.words: Volume is the spine. Phase, dominant domain, prey, HUD all key off per-domain VOLUME (Cell.LiveVolume), not prism count.
entries.rule: Everything about a cell (phase, dominant domain, prey, HUD) keys off per-domain laid volume, never prism count (count is only a frenzy/perf backstop); a change that moves laid volume re-measures the cell's phase ladder.
entries.test: Does any threshold or read in the design use prism count instead of volume, and does a generator change re-measure the ladder?

entries.words: Node control is the NUCLEUS: in a cell with a nucleus, DominantDomain reads only the per-domain ENVIRONMENT volume laid inside the nucleus (the territorial claim — a fauna sanctuary players contest with abilities + out-laying volume); everything outside is the voraciously-grazed feeding ground and never sways control.
entries.rule: In a nucleus cell, control is the volume laid inside the nucleus and the outside is contested feeding ground that never sways control; a mode that borrows the nucleus as play geometry declares it is not a control zone rather than bending the rule.
entries.test: Where is control read in the design, and if the nucleus is repurposed, is NucleusIsControlZone set off?

entries.words: Every lifeform drops one elemental crystal (Charge/Mass/Space/Time) as a powerup on death, enforced by LifeFormCrystal. It must not be possible to make a lifeform that violates this.
entries.rule: Every lifeform carries one elemental heart and drops it on death; in a colony every member is a lifeform with its own heart and only the root is heartless.
entries.retired: the "body segments are body-parts and carry none" ruling (retracted)
entries.test: Does every lifeform in the design drop exactly one crystal on death?

entries.words: Flora have POPULATIONS too, and a plant's feeding is GROWTH. Flora are not scenery that a timer keeps extruding: like fauna they have a seed floor, a hard per-cell cap and reproduction as the population driver
entries.rule: Plants are a population: a seed floor, a per-cell cap resolved on the Cell, and reproduction funded by the prisms a plant grew; spawners only seed, and a lowered cap stops producing and never culls.
entries.test: Is the plant population driven by reproduction and bounded by the Cell's cap, with no timer and no cull?

entries.words: A lattice species grows on its SURFACE'S OWN TILE, never on a fitted grid.
entries.rule: A lattice plant grows on the exact tiling its surface carries, never on a fitted Euclidean grid; a function-shaped surface with no tiling addresses on the sphere instead.
entries.retired: the marching-walk approximation across a minimal surface
entries.test: Does the new species grow on its surface's own tile or on a grid fitted to it?

entries.words: Territorial permanence. Take a cell, leave, it stays yours — the claim fauna cannot touch.
entries.rule: A claimed nucleus is never consumed by fauna, so a cell taken stays taken when you leave; only the exterior is contested churn.
entries.test: Can anything in the design erode a claimed nucleus while its owner is away? Then it fails.

entries.words: TIME breeds faster — the second elemental law. A Time plant reproduces at 1.25x the fleet rate and Charge/Mass/Space at 0.8x
entries.rule: Tempo is Time's identity: a Time plant reproduces fastest (1.25x against 0.8x), and the rate is resolved from the element at spawn, never authored per config.
entries.test: Does Time breed fastest in the species, and is the rate derived from the element rather than typed per asset?

entries.words: THE FOUR ELEMENTAL IDENTITIES OF A PLANT — one rule, and a species does not get to invent them. CHARGE makes every prism danger ... MASS is ARMOURED and its shield carries its volume ... SPACE is the highest ASPECT RATIO ... TIME is the fastest clock
entries.rule: A species authors one leaf and the four elements spend it four ways (Charge danger, Mass armoured at x0.64 under Space, Space the longest aspect, Time the fastest clock); the four are a redistribution averaging exactly 1, never an inflation, so no cell's volume ladder moves.
entries.test: Does the species type its own element forms, or does one authored leaf take the fleet law with multipliers averaging 1?

entries.words: Endogenous selection only. When evolution lands, fitness is survival itself (starvation/predation/reproduction cost), never a designer-scored fitness function
entries.rule: Fitness is survival itself (starvation, predation, reproduction cost), never a designer-scored function; this is the line between artificial life and an optimizer.
entries.test: Does any evolution or selection in the design score lifeforms with a hand-written fitness function? It fails.

entries.words: LEVEL IS RETIRED — a lifeform is its species and its ELEMENT, and nothing else.
entries.rule: No per-individual acquired growth of any kind: feeding pays out as population (a reset starvation clock, a birth, a growth quota), never as a bigger individual, and offspring inherit only the element.
entries.retired: the spawn-time level roll (LifeformLevelSpread) and the earned level (FeedsPerLevel, InitialLevel, BodyScalePerLevel, LeafScalePerLevel)
entries.test: Do two creatures of one species and element ever differ in size or power for reasons only the simulation knows? Then it fails.

entries.words: A world you load is opt-in, and swapping one is ACTIVE removal — not decay. ... Do not turn this into anything that runs on its own: no auto-rotate, no idle re-roll, no "the cell has been up too long" reset.
entries.rule: A world swap suctions the old cell out and blooms the new one in only because a player flew into a station and asked; nothing swaps or resets a world on its own.
entries.test: Does any world change in the design happen without an explicit player act? Then it is the timed culler in a costume.

entries.words: direct abilities should only steal or strip (for recollection), but if a player produces danger prisms that is a way for them to remove crystals from the environment.
entries.rule: A direct ability only steals or strips petals, which stay recollectable in the world; only a danger prism burns crystals out of the match, and control theft is never an economy form.
entries.retired: the danger-prism control mute on the Sparrow and Grizzly (EventOnVesselSlowedByRhinoDangerPrism, deleted 2026-10-17)
entries.test: Does the ability's hit do anything to a rival other than steal or strip petals, or burn them through a danger prism? If yes it is out.

entries.words: the scale of the elemental crystals in the conversion animation found in the ark is the perfect size for elemental crystals. lets fix all elemental crystals to that one size and have them grant exactly one petal.
entries.rule: Every elemental crystal is one size (the Ark converter's) and grants exactly one petal; the omni crystal is one size too.
entries.retired: variable crystal sizes and multi-petal crystals
entries.test: Does the design spawn a crystal of another size or worth? If yes it breaks one size, one petal.

entries.words: Elementals — the single system that governs all buffing and debuffing across vessels and their environment. If a buff or debuff isn't expressed through elementals, that's a smell.
entries.rule: Every buff and debuff on a vessel or its environment is a change of elemental level; nothing else buffs or debuffs.
entries.test: Is every buff/debuff in the design an element level change (petals)? A stat modifier outside the elementals fails.

entries.words: A vessel DEBUFF is a TRANSFER, not a decay (Docs/ELEMENTAL_ECONOMY.md): it moves petals permanently out of the victim's base level and into one of three places — stolen by the attacker on a contact verb, ejected as free-for-all crystals on any ranged verb, or burned by a hostile danger prism, which is the economy's only sink.
entries.rule: A debuff moves petals permanently out of the victim (stolen on contact, ejected as crystals on a ranged verb, burned by a danger prism, the only sink); a buff is temporary; lifeform reproduction and spawning are the only source of petals; nothing partial leaves and nothing is minted.
entries.test: For every petal the design moves, say where it came from and where it goes; a permanent buff or a petal from nowhere fails.

entries.words: Collecting one is a BEAT, not a journey — snatch → suction → absorb in 0.44 s ... a mode's objective must never wait on a flourish
entries.rule: A crystal pickup is one shared 0.44 s beat from the one config, never a per-prefab duration; the reward and the scoring event land at contact, and no objective waits on a flourish.
entries.retired: per-prefab capture durations (1 s on two fauna, 3 s on eleven flora)
entries.test: Does the reward land at contact and does the pickup read the same length whichever hull took it?

entries.words: There is no XP — quest completion is the only currency.
entries.rule: Progression has no XP; completing quests is the only thing that unlocks vessels, modes and intensities.
entries.test: Does the design introduce points, levels or XP as a progression currency? It fails.

entries.words: ONE BLAST PAYS A VICTIM ONCE, and the per-blast ledger is what enforces it.
entries.rule: A single blast scores and drains a victim once, however many times they re-enter it over its life.
entries.test: Can a victim be paid twice by one shot in the design? Then it fails.

entries.words: The maintained-mechanism law (LOCKED). No sustained/held mechanism may HOLD an element above integer level 10 — the 10..15 overcharge band belongs to transients only, and everything in it drains back to (at most) 10
entries.rule: No sustained or held mechanism keeps an element above level 10; the 10-15 overcharge band is for transients that drain back, so the player feels every reward above 10 and the headroom always returns.
entries.retired: the domain fauna buff (living fauna hearts empowering their whole domain's vessels, removed Sep 2026)
entries.test: Can anything in the design hold an element above 10 for as long as a condition lasts? It fails.

entries.words: Create FTUE mpckups - look at the old desing the captain/pilot shouldcome from the side and guidethe players
entries.rule: First-time guidance is given by a captain or pilot character who enters from the side and speaks to the player, with a leader line to the one lit control; not a bare caption strip.
entries.retired: the Rev 21 caption-strip guide
entries.test: Does the FTUE step show a pilot who is here with the player and points at the one control, rather than text alone?

entries.words: Guide, don't carry (LOCKED on the training branch, `Docs/HomeHub/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 there): to send a player somewhere, spotlight the one control to press next, dim and disable the rest, never take Settings away, and let the player press it themselves.
entries.rule: To send a player somewhere, spotlight the one control to press next, dim and disable everything else except Settings, and let them press it; never navigate for them.
entries.retired: the first-login railroad that opened screens for the player
entries.test: Does any guidance open a screen, press a control or move the player on their behalf? If yes it carries instead of guiding.

entries.words: C1 — XP REMOVED ENTIRELY. Quest completion is the only progression currency. No XP storage, display, award, or gating.
entries.rule: There is no XP: quest completion is the only progression currency.
entries.retired: XP storage, display, awards and gating (ParticipationXpAwarder, XPTrackView)
entries.test: Does the design store, show, award or gate on XP? If yes it is out.

entries.words: C2 — SINGLE GUIDANCE CHANNEL. Every in-app "go here / do this" hint routes through the CTA/breadcrumb system, driven solely by `GameModeProgressionService`.
entries.rule: Every 'go here / do this' hint is the one breadcrumb channel; exactly one frontier breadcrumb is live at a time.
entries.test: Does the design add a second hint, arrow, toast or pointer outside the breadcrumb system?

entries.words: C3 — CONTINUITY LAW. CTA indicators bloom/grow on activate and wither/fade on dismiss — they never pop instantly into or out of existence.
entries.rule: A call-to-action indicator blooms on activate and withers on dismiss; nothing pops into or out of existence.
entries.test: Does any hint or indicator appear or vanish in one frame?

entries.words: C4 — UNLOCKS PERSISTENT & MONOTONIC. Once revealed, a feature stays unlocked across sessions
entries.rule: Once a feature is revealed it stays unlocked across sessions; unlocks never regress.
entries.test: Can any flow re-lock or hide a feature the player already unlocked?

entries.words: GUIDE A PLAYER BY SHOWING THE PATH, NEVER BY WALKING IT (LOCKED rule — every quest, tutorial and onboarding beat).
entries.rule: To send a player somewhere, spotlight the one control to press next, dim and disable everything else except Settings, and let the player press each step themselves; nothing opens a screen, selects a card, presses a button or flies the vessel on their behalf.
entries.retired: the first-login railroad (TrySelectMode, ArmForcedEntry) and the Quest Graph's Navigate / EnterFreestyle nodes
entries.test: Does any onboarding step navigate, select or fly for the player? Then it fails; each step must be a spotlight the player presses.

entries.words: Later we are going to want to learn the course for regatta that minimizes the disparity between the fastest and the slowest AI flying different vessels trained on their respective time Arcade games. Then ... we will learn the minimal elemental tuning needed to close that gap.
entries.rule: Regatta is balanced in three stages: train each hull's AI in its own Time games, search the course that minimises the fastest-to-slowest gap between those AIs, then the smallest elemental tuning that closes the rest, which becomes the vessels' mobility baseline.
entries.test: Does a Regatta balance change come from the course search against trained AIs before any elemental tuning, and is the tuning the smallest that closes the gap?

entries.words: estimate new score requirements etc. for arcade games such that experienced players are finishing at around the 90 seconds mark
entries.rule: Every arcade mode's end-game target is set so an experienced player finishes at about 90 seconds; a mode with no timed playtest carries an estimate until one is flown.
entries.test: Does the mode's target (score, laps, gates) put an experienced run near 90 s at intensity 1?

entries.words: make every vessel's Time game fun, because it is what makes the vessel fun to fly between places on a voyage. Score each one, then raise the floors.
entries.rule: Every vessel's Time game must be fun in itself (verb, flow, ladder, feedback, ...), because it is how the vessel feels to fly between places on a voyage; score it and raise its weakest dimension first.
entries.test: Score the Time game on the six dimensions: is its floor the thing the design raises, and is the hull's own speed verb the way to win?

entries.words: go ahead and fix tandava etc.
entries.rule: A mode's world is scaled round the fleet-law creature body (Tandava inherits the Swarm's scaled body; its reef, cell and meals grow to fit), never the creature pinned back to fit the mode.
entries.retired: Tandava's pinned research body
entries.test: Does the mode override a lifeform's body, heart gap or element scale to fit its arena? If yes, scale the arena instead.

entries.words: Stoat will use Slingshot and Meerkat will use Warpline. These will be two time game modes of these two vessels.
entries.rule: Slingshot is the Stoat's Time race and Warpline the Meerkat's; each is shaped for its one hull.
entries.retired: Warpline as the Stoat's Time race (before 2026-10-27)
entries.test: Does the design seat the Stoat in Warpline or the Meerkat in Slingshot, or give either race a second hull? If yes it is off the map.

entries.words: "make every vessel's time game very fun"
entries.rule: Every hull has its own Time race, authored to be very fun around what that hull alone does well.
entries.test: Does the hull have a Time card, and does the race turn on the hull's own movement rather than a generic circuit?

entries.words: Serpent Time (shown as Serpentine since 2026-10-31) is the dirty race
entries.rule: Serpentine's gates are single rings closed by mode-laid shapes with a gold core, ringed by regrowing debris that feeds Seed Walls; the mode is dirty through its track and AI while the vessel is never changed.
entries.retired: the rounds economy and the walls' speed cost (built and retired 2026-10-31)
entries.test: Does the Serpentine design add difficulty through gates, debris and AI only, with no change to the Serpent's kit?

entries.words: A game mode never changes the vessel (LOCKED rule, Shombith, 2026-10-31) ... "The vessel kit as designed always stays the same, we just make the game mode interesting."
entries.rule: A mode makes itself interesting with its track, environment and AI only; it never rations, vetoes, rescales, adds contact effects to, or edits what a vessel's abilities do; a kit change is a vessel change for the vessel's owner.
entries.retired: Serpent Time's crystal-bought sniper rounds and its walls that cost speed (built 2026-10-27, retired 2026-10-31)
entries.test: List every way the mode touches a vessel's abilities, presses, contact effects or numbers; the list must be empty.

entries.words: "it can paint at two places where there is prism mass clusters ... so he can in a way paint its path and zoom towards it"
entries.rule: The Angler's Time race is about painting prism clusters and dashing to them: two neutral clusters per leg on the ring's own axis, the second dash through the ring, the ladder being where the paint is.
entries.test: Does the course give the Angler clusters to paint and dash to on every leg?

entries.words: I want a plan that gonna introduce the new player to the time ability of Manta in intensity 1, and in intensity 4, it will get to intense. No other elemental abilities needed, only time.
entries.rule: A vessel's Time game teaches its Time ability alone: introduced gently at I1 and intense at I4, with no corner or gate that needs another element.
entries.test: Does any level of the Time game need an ability other than Time to pass, or does I1 already demand the full ability? Either breaks the ladder.

entries.words: Brittle Star Time is four movement questions, one per intensity
entries.rule: Brittle Star Time asks one movement question per intensity (I1 Gearbox, I2 Feather slalom, I3 Coast-in hairpins, I4 Corkscrew), 8 rings x 2 laps on every rung.
entries.test: Does each intensity of the race ask a different movement question of the hull rather than only adding hazards?

entries.words: Ecology must be opt-out-able per mode (a race may want sparse life) but present by default.
entries.rule: Ecology is present in every mode by default; a mode may thin it (a race may want sparse life) but never builds a world without it unless it opts out on purpose.
entries.test: Does the mode's cell carry life by default, and is any absence of ecology an explicit opt-out rather than an omission?

entries.words: The Cell owns the environment — minigames must not build parallel systems (LOCKED best-practice)
entries.rule: The Cell is every mode's environment: boundary, atmosphere, population and crystals come from the CellConfigDataSO and its spawn profile, never from a mode-local boundary cage, particle system or spawner.
entries.test: Does the mode build its own playfield edge, motes, life or crystal spawner? If yes it duplicates the Cell.

entries.words: A toy has no score and no end condition — something to play with indefinitely (toys are to freestyle what party games are to the rest of Cosmic Shore).
entries.rule: A toy is a world-space station flown into in freestyle with no score, no end condition, no timer and no decay; it composes with the fundamentals (vessel, domain, elementals, cell, mass) and declares a category (Pilot, World, Creation) by what it does.
entries.test: Does the toy keep score, end, or run a clock? Then it is a mode, not a toy; and which of the three categories does it reach for?

entries.words: before a mode builds a set of points of interest, check whether the platform already grows one.
entries.rule: A mode anchors its points of interest on what the platform already grows (living flora hearts in FloraHeartRegistry) before authoring sockets of its own, so the set is alive, grazeable and joustable.
entries.retired: Tollway's own set of sockets
entries.test: Does the mode author fixed points where the food web already grows a set?

entries.words: The Cell owns the environment — minigames don't build parallel systems.
entries.rule: A mode that needs ecology wires and configures the standard Cell (membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, spawn profile, phase thresholds in volume) and owns only its gameplay-bearing structure; no mode-local spawner, culler, edge cage or plankton, and never a hand-placed membrane, nucleus or cytoplasm.
entries.test: List every environment piece the mode builds; each must be either a Cell config or gameplay-bearing (a wall a ball bounces off, a goal, a ring).

entries.words: a card's Vessels list is the authority on what a mode admits; the hangar lock gates the hangar
entries.rule: A card's Vessels list alone decides which hulls a mode offers; the hangar's purchase lock gates only the hangar.
entries.retired: filtering the arena carousel by SO_Vessel.IsLocked
entries.test: Does anything but the card's Vessels list filter a mode's carousel?

entries.words: A hit is priced by its VERB, never by its hull
entries.rule: Combat points price the verb (a round 1, a contact strike 8, an area debuff 12, a rocket 10/20/30), never the hull, so a card can gain a hull without the scoring rule learning anything.
entries.test: Does the scoring path name any hull? It fails; it names verbs only.

entries.words: a brawl is more balanceable than a race, because the mode owns the windows
entries.rule: A mode balances through what it owns (hit windows, prices, cooldowns), never through vessel speed, which a card cannot touch.
entries.test: Which levers does the balance plan pull? Any lever on a vessel's own numbers fails.

entries.words: A teleport threads NOTHING, and the rule is the platform's rather than the mode's
entries.rule: A teleport never threads a ring or gate; a step containing one counts no gate, in every mode.
entries.test: Can a wormhole or jump in the design count a gate it skipped? It fails.

entries.words: when i am flying in freestyle with a multi seat vessel any other player in freestyle should be able to press left or right on the dpad, or use a two finger swipe on mobile, to change seats ... there should be no difference between a vessel spawned in and a vessel abandoned by switching.
entries.rule: In freestyle (and a running arena match) every player on a domain cycles its seats across every hull with D-pad left/right (a two-finger swipe on a phone); the AI flies every seat no person holds, and a hull abandoned by switching is exactly as free as one the spawner added.
entries.test: Can a player reach every free seat on their domain with one cycle gesture, and does leaving a hull hand it to an AI with nothing spawned or destroyed?

entries.words: we liked the old plasma kind design for the lobby with connected tree but it locked it for 4 players only do something where it is expandable with the host and its there, also decrease the tone of the blue a little bit on the bg
entries.rule: The party lobby draws the connected molecule with the host at its centre and grows with the party beyond four; the blue background stays toned down.
entries.test: Does the lobby show every member bonded to the host and keep working past four players?

entries.words: that issue is true for any vessel swapping situation ... it should be resolved.
entries.rule: A hull's element levels and latched level-5 unlocks travel with the hull on every hand-over (arena pilot swap, crew seat change, duel swap), never with the machine that last simulated it.
entries.test: Does every new hand-over of a hull between players or AIs carry its element levels across? If a player could lose collected petals by swapping, it is wrong.

entries.words: The two LOCKED party decisions (two-level presence lobby + party session, eager per-user Relay) are given
entries.rule: The party is a two-level presence lobby plus party session with an eager per-user Relay: every player hosts their own Relay-backed party session on entering the menu; lazy, on-first-invite creation must not return.
entries.retired: lazy / on-first-invite Relay creation
entries.test: Does the design create Relay lazily, merge the two lobby levels, or bypass the party session?

entries.words: A PILOT'S DOMAIN PICK WIDENS THE MATCH, up to the mode's own limit.
entries.rule: A pilot's domain pick is honoured by widening the active domain set up to the mode's limit; no pick is silently reassigned at spawn.
entries.retired: NormalizeUnassignedHumans reassigning a picked domain at spawn
entries.test: Can a pick the launch UI accepted be changed at spawn? It fails.

entries.words: Single scene: Do not create separate singleplayer/multiplayer scenes. AI backfill handles solo play within the same Netcode pipeline.
entries.rule: Solo play is the multiplayer pipeline with AI backfill; a mode never ships separate single-player and multiplayer scenes.
entries.test: Does the mode design a solo scene or path of its own? It fails.

entries.words: we are very GPU bottlenecked on mobile ... we need to create the medium and low setting to also shift some of that burden off the GPU
entries.rule: Quality presets must cut real GPU work on phones (sky, AA, HDR, bloom, render scale, overdraw), not only Unity's quality level.
entries.test: Does each preset step measurably lower GPU time on a phone? A preset that changes nothing a phone GPU pays for is not a preset.

entries.words: the keyboard controls should mirror the others and just have a consistent cycle left and right
entries.rule: The keyboard mirrors the pad: one consistent cycle left and right; no key picks a seat outright.
entries.retired: the Orca's 1-4 and the Wrasse's 1 / 2 seat keys
entries.test: Does a keyboard binding select a seat directly instead of cycling? If yes it diverges from the pad.

entries.words: Touch first (Garrett, 2026-10-25: controls for 2D characters are mobile, then gamepad, then mouse/keyboard)
entries.rule: Controls for a 2D seat are designed for touch first, then gamepad, then mouse and keyboard.
entries.test: Is the touch control the first one designed and the richest, with pad and keyboard mirroring it?

entries.words: 0 to 0.3 - subtle by design (Garrett 2026-10-27)
entries.rule: A drift is felt as a subtle rumble (haptic 0 to 0.3 following the slip angle; a fine camera rumble) and never more.
entries.test: Does a drift shake, displace or buzz hard? It is subtle by design.

entries.words: The pad binding was LB + RB together. The shoulders now belong to the pilot: LB opens the pilot's sight and RB is proposed for the payload
entries.rule: The shoulders belong to the pilot (LB the pilot's sight, RB the payload); the rear view is D-pad down, and no chord may overlap them.
entries.retired: the LB + RB rear-view chord
entries.test: Does a new binding use LB, RB or D-pad down, or a chord of them? If yes it collides with the pilot's shoulders.

entries.words: I want it exactly like Overwatch 2 ... the entire scene need to be the actual scene ... every single prism, every single game object
entries.rule: A replay plays the match in its real scene from the recorded path and actions, every prism and object, with skip-back by reload and fast-forward; the player's last 10 games are kept on the device.
entries.test: Does the replay draw the real scene with every object, or a stand-in?

entries.words: the Meerkat's wormhole is now a Soliton Tunnel, an environmental fundamental any vessel or scene can use
entries.rule: The soliton tunnel is an environmental fundamental any vessel or scene can use, not a Meerkat-only ability effect.
entries.test: Does a new tunnel, portal or ride reuse the Soliton Tunnel rather than a bespoke one?

entries.words: "change the lavalamp default vessel from meerkat to squirrel"
entries.rule: The lava lamp and freestyle spawn the Squirrel by default.
entries.retired: the Meerkat as the menu hull (2026-10-28, one day)
entries.test: Does the menu still spawn the Squirrel unless the Vessel Changer swaps it?

entries.words: Cosmic Shore ships two everyday haptic feels, both local-human-pilot-only, plus one rare alert reserved for match-changing events and one continuous texture fenced to a held full-auto trigger. Everything else is deliberately silent.
entries.rule: Haptics are minimal and legible: a skim pulse (reward), a punish thud (mistake), one rare alert for match-changing events and fenced textures for a held trigger; everything else is silent and nothing fights.
entries.test: Does the design add a buzz to a UI tap, boost, joust or explosion? If yes it is noise.

entries.words: Blue is the "no team / not yet picked / neutral entity" sentinel and is never present in GameDataSO.ActiveDomains (the playable set is {Jade, Ruby, Gold}, indices 0..2).
entries.rule: There are three playable domains (Jade, Ruby, Gold); Blue means no team / neutral and is never a player's domain.
entries.retired: Domains.None and Domains.Unassigned
entries.test: Does the design put a pilot on Blue or add a fourth playable domain? Either fails.

entries.words: Two everyday feels, both local-human-pilot-only (skim-pulse reward + prism-punish thud), plus one rare alert shake fenced to match-changing events
entries.rule: Haptics are two everyday feels for the local human pilot (skim reward, prism punish), one rare alert shake for match-changing events, one spray buzz for a held full-auto trigger and one bind grind; everything else is silent and a texture never cuts off an event.
entries.test: Does the design add a haptic outside these five, or one that fires for an AI or remote pilot? It fails.

entries.words: Cosmic Shore aims to be built on a small, carefully curated set of fundamentals whose interactions produce a large number of desirable emergent outcomes.
entries.rule: A design works through the fundamentals (Domain, Mass, Cells, Elementals, Prisms, Prism movement, Flora & Fauna, Vessels, Toys, Switch, Lit, Ark, Soliton), never around them; a feature that composes with none is a bespoke solution.
entries.test: Name the fundamentals the feature composes with and how; if it names none, it is bespoke and needs the owner's sign-off.

entries.words: Domain — team/affiliation identity attached to mass, vessels, and structures. Sometimes referred to casually as "color"; the canonical term is domain.
entries.rule: Team identity is Domain, attached to mass, vessels and structures; "color" is only the casual word, never a second system.
entries.test: Does every owned thing in the design carry a Domain, and is team expressed through it rather than a parallel notion?

entries.words: Switch — a ring you thread, and threading it activates something.
entries.rule: The one word for "this does something when you go through it" is Switch: a ring threaded by a vessel or a ball; it composes with toys, prisms, domain and cells rather than duplicating any of them.
entries.test: Is every go-through activation in the design a switch ring, not a new trigger shape?

entries.words: Three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction, but a bespoke feature that duplicates or bypasses an existing fundamental is worse than either.
entries.rule: Solve in this order and stop at the first fit: use an existing fundamental, tune its parameters, extend it, propose a new fundamental (with explicit sign-off), and only last a bespoke solution.
entries.test: State which rung of the order the design sits on and why each lower rung was rejected.

entries.words: If the most direct path to a goal would require reaching past the fundamentals and using privileged information or a shortcut to explicitly produce the outcome, stop and ask the prompter for explicit permission before doing so.
entries.rule: Never hard-code an outcome the fundamentals should produce; a shortcut that reads privileged state or scripts the result needs the owner's explicit permission first, with the emergent alternative described.
entries.test: Does any part of the design read placement or hidden state to produce the result directly? Then it is a cheat and needs sign-off.

entries.words: The HyperSea has rules and everything in it follows them — game scenes, Menu_Main's lava-lamp/freestyle, tools and test scenes alike. Do not create context-specific exemptions
entries.rule: One HyperSea, one rule set: no "only the menu", "just cosmetic" or "perf special case" carve-outs; build a system once and use it everywhere, and treat a context the universal systems cannot serve as a fundamentals discussion, not a local workaround.
entries.test: Does the brief ask for any rule to be off in one scene, mode or device tier? Then it needs the owner's explicit grant.

entries.words: Naming: "lava lamp" and "freestyle" are the same thing.
entries.rule: The menu's lava lamp and freestyle are one system: the autopilot vessel behind the menu is the one the player flies, and every rule holds there; there is no standalone Freestyle mode.
entries.retired: the standalone Freestyle arcade game (GameModes 7) and MultiplayerFreestyle (28), removed 2026-10-08
entries.test: Does the design treat the menu vessel or world as cosmetic or separate from freestyle? It fails.

entries.words: No prism may ever need multiframe CPU updates in order to animate. ... Colliders — and gameplay state generally — go to the FINAL state at the START of the animation. Only photons animate.
entries.rule: A prism's gameplay state (collider, ownership, cell sums) is final the frame an animation starts; only its photons animate, off a stamped GPU clock, with no CPU-driven multi-frame animation and no legacy fallback.
entries.retired: CPU animation managers and per-material fallback tiers (strict mode: no legacy fallback)
entries.test: Does any prism effect leave gameplay state mid-transition or need per-frame CPU writes to animate? If yes it breaks the clock-material law.

entries.words: The FIFO trail cap breaks a LOCKED rule. (Resolved 2026-10-05: the owner granted it for MobileLow only - decision 4, §3.6; the paragraph below is the analysis that asked for it.)
entries.rule: The Skim Race and Joust FIFO trail cap is an authorised exception to 'no trail caps', fenced to the MobileLow tier and those two modes only; nowhere else may a trail be capped.
entries.test: Does a trail cap or oldest-prism consumption appear outside MobileLow Skim Race and Joust? If yes it is forbidden.

entries.words: the rhino and stoat have introduced prism movement. prism movement should be a fundamental with consistent expectations. one of them should be that when a moving prism collides with another prism both prism should be destroyed.
entries.rule: Prism movement is one fundamental with the same expectations for every mover: a moving (force-displaced) prism that runs into another prism destroys both, through the ordinary destruction path, scored to the force behind the motion.
entries.test: Does anything new that moves prisms run its own collision rule instead of PrismMotion's? If yes, it is a bespoke duplicate of the fundamental.

entries.words: make a variety of prisms collisions that use the ultra high res prism used by slicing. these should look spectacular when looked at but undistinguished from the normal explosion when squinting. when we can afford it use those for level one and turn it off on level 2.
entries.rule: A prism collision up close is spectacular (the ultra-high-res cut), paid for through a ladder that drops to the plain explosion as moving prisms multiply; the look follows the viewer's distance and the budget, never a per-mode choice.
entries.retired: the 'undistinguished from the normal explosion when squinting' half (retired by the designer on 2026-10-16)
entries.test: Does the destruction look come from the shared distance ladder (showcase, plain, bulk) rather than a bespoke per-feature effect?

entries.words: "we don't want to bloat our run time load when this is a strictly editor time solvable problem ... don't reduce prism count. minimally reduce scale so they are flush."
entries.rule: No generated prism interpenetrates another; it is held at authoring time inside each generator by sizing prisms flush with their neighbours (never by removing prisms and never by a runtime pass).
entries.test: Does the generator's own lay list clip (audit_prism_clipping.py), and is any fix a scale change at authoring rather than a runtime pass or a count cut?

entries.words: the stealing effect is supposed to curl the original domain and reveal the stolen domain underneath, but i am seeing it immediately change domain color and the peel the changed color to have the changed color also underneath
entries.rule: A steal peels the OLD domain's skin off the prism to reveal the NEW domain underneath; the outside never changes colour abruptly, and the only new colour on screen is what the curl uncovers.
entries.test: In a steal or domain change, is the old colour what peels and the new colour what is revealed, with no abrupt recolour of the outside?

entries.words: lets use the silver gnomen triangles that are used on the explosion shader on the suction shader. Use the same LOD system as well.
entries.rule: Every prism death speaks one language: consumption (suction) is drawn with the destruction's silver-gnomon cut and the same distance LOD ladder, not a separate effect.
entries.retired: the SuctionGraph implosion as the consumption look
entries.test: Does a new way of removing a prism reuse the destruction's cut, fragments and LOD ladder instead of its own effect?

entries.words: lets have prisms move and be dragged by the net. they should only be destroyed when they collide with other prisms
entries.rule: A prism carried by a mover (the Jacks' net) stays a live moving prism and dies only by the collision rule, never by being carried.
entries.test: Does carrying, dragging or throwing a prism destroy or consume it on its own? If yes, the prism must live until the collision rule takes it.

entries.words: change the fundamental movement interaction of prisms (effecting all shielded prism movement), so shielded prisms bounce off each other and other prisms instead of being destroyed on collision.
entries.rule: A collision a shielded prism is part of, as the mover or as the prism hit, destroys neither: the movers rebound (restitution 0.6); only plain-on-plain annihilates, and a plain mover dies against super-shielded mass.
entries.retired: shielded prisms destroyed on prism-on-prism collision (expectation 1 as applied to shielded prisms before 2026-10-27)
entries.test: Does the design destroy a shielded prism in a prism-on-prism collision, or let a mover pass through one? If yes it breaks the LOCKED bounce rule.

entries.words: a moving prism that runs into another prism destroys BOTH — scored to the force behind the motion, devastating
entries.rule: A prism a force displaces is a moving prism, and every moving prism meets the world by one rule: running into another prism destroys both, scored to the force behind the motion, with no friendly exception; a prism posed by its owner every frame (a creature's body, a growing plant, a projectile payload) is not a mover.
entries.test: Does any new force that moves mass call PrismMotion rather than its own contact test, and does its collision destroy both prisms (own wall included)?

entries.words: (Garrett, 2026-10-27; LOCKED 2026-10-28): a collision a SHIELDED prism is part of, mover or struck, destroys neither, and the movers rebound off the contact
entries.rule: A collision a shielded prism is part of, as mover or struck, destroys neither prism; the movers bounce off the contact.
entries.test: Trace a shielded prism through the design's collisions: it must survive and the mover must rebound.

entries.words: CLAUDE.md's danger-prism rule is LOCKED: danger prisms are not safe to their own domain, and a danger-prism effect must not GATE on domain.
entries.rule: A danger prism punishes every vessel that touches it, its own domain included; the prism's domain only chooses how the loss lands (opposing-domain danger burns crystals out of the match, own-domain danger is the temporary debuff), never whether an effect runs.
entries.test: Does any danger-prism effect skip or gate on the toucher's domain? If yes it breaks the LOCKED rule.

entries.words: Mass is conserved: it has no passive decay. A prism (the concrete unit of mass), once created, is only ever removed by an active force — a vessel using an ability, or fauna eating it.
entries.rule: A prism leaves the world only through an active force (a vessel ability or fauna eating it); there is no aging, lifespan, timed culler or decay oscillator anywhere, in every scene the simulation runs in, the menu lava lamp included.
entries.test: List every path that removes a prism in the design; each must be an ability or consumption, never a clock, cap or TTL.

entries.words: Prisms / Prismscapes — the geometric primitive of player-generated structure. Trails are the 1-dimensional case of a prismscape; higher-dimensional prism constructions reuse this primitive rather than introducing parallel structure types.
entries.rule: All player-built structure is prisms on one dimension ladder (0D singleton, 1D trail, 2D surface, 3D volume); a vessel that attaches rides 1D or 2D, 0D is deliberately not rideable, and a prismscape constrains position only, never the pilot's attitude.
entries.test: Does the feature build with prisms on the ladder rather than a new structure type, and does riding leave attitude to the pilot?

entries.words: super-shielded mass is never destroyed: it deflects, an unshielded mover goes against it and a shielded one bounces, and no force moves it in the first place
entries.rule: Super-shielded mass is never destroyed and never moved: it deflects movers.
entries.test: Can anything in the design destroy or displace super-shielded mass? Then it fails.

entries.words: there is no context in which trail caps, prism TTLs, or idle cullers are acceptable.
