entries.rule: No trail cap, prism TTL or idle culler anywhere, the menu included; perf pressure is solved by fauna cleanup or by pausing the spawner (not creating mass is allowed, aging it out is not); the only granted exceptions are the Wanderway rolling tether and the MobileLow Skim Race / Joust trail cap (2026-10-05), each by explicit sign-off.
entries.retired: the menu trail ring-buffer cap (maxTrailBlocks / Trail.RemoveOldest, commit 64d8f0c8, reverted)
entries.test: Does the design age mass out in any context? It fails unless it is one of the two recorded exceptions.

entries.words: Dynamic contact never does nothing
entries.rule: A mover that touches a prism it cannot affect still acknowledges the hit: own armoured mass lights, super-shielded mass jiggles.
entries.test: For every contact the design cannot resolve as destruction, what does the player see? Nothing fails.

entries.words: Danger prisms are not safe to their own domain (locked design). IsDangerous effects apply to every vessel that touches the prism, regardless of domain — friendly fire included
entries.rule: A danger prism hurts every vessel that touches it, its own domain included; danger and both shield tiers are mutually exclusive.
entries.test: Does any danger-prism effect gate on domain, or does any prism carry danger and a shield at once? Either fails.

entries.words: A prism's DEATH VISUAL wears the palette of the TIER it was wearing, never just its domain.
entries.rule: Debris from a dying prism is tinted from the tier it wore (plain, shielded, danger), never from its domain alone.
entries.test: Does a danger or shielded prism shatter into debris that still reads as that tier?

entries.words: For all vessels when I tap their ability's icon/element totem it should be the same as using the glyph input.
entries.rule: On a phone, tapping an ability card presses that ability exactly like its glyph input (finger down presses, finger up releases), on every vessel.
entries.test: Does every ability card press its ability on touch, and does a hold on the card hold the ability?

entries.words: Every card is its ability's button (2026-10-19, Garrett). A finger on a pressable card presses the control its chip names and lifting releases
entries.rule: On touch a pressable ability card is the control its chip names (press and release); locked, passive and gesture cards are not pressable, and a touch that starts on a card is never a flight thumb.
entries.test: Does tapping a card press exactly the control its chip names, and does the flight thumb ignore touches that start on a card?

entries.words: a very subtle camera shake on the onset and ... a subtle danger colored vignette that fits the game's aesthetics to signal the silenced state on all vessels
entries.rule: The silenced pilot feels the onset (a subtle shake, and a lighter one per further hit) and sees the state held for the whole window as a danger-coloured edge, on every hull.
entries.test: Does a new debuff state land with a felt onset and a held, subtle, danger-coloured signal on every hull, rather than a one-off cue?

entries.words: the pull plus the 2d edge is very strong effect. lets try that on relatively thin edge around screen with high resolution. the more seconds of silence the deeper it goes in and bleeds back out as the seconds drain
entries.rule: The silence perimeter's depth follows the seconds left: a thin high-resolution edge with little silence, deeper as hits add seconds, bleeding back out as they drain.
entries.test: Does the effect's intensity read the state's remaining duration, so a player can tell how long it holds without a timer?

entries.words: each of the orca turrets needs two buttons: fire gun, fire missiles. it does these with the right thumb and aims with the left. it has all the info it needs now. it no longer needs the ui breaking top row of text, unique to that vessel.
entries.rule: A gunner seat is two buttons under the right thumb with aim on the left, and no vessel gets a UI-breaking text row unique to itself.
entries.retired: the Orca's seat line (the top row of text)
entries.test: Does a seat need text to be understood, or more than two fire buttons?

entries.words: if the lowest graphics setting are selected don't display pips. start the player in the wrasse and the ratel. in this setting very little of the game should even need to be processed, so the ratel should run fine on very old phones
entries.rule: On Very Low only one view renders: crew picture-in-picture views are off and the player flies one seat, so the game runs on very old phones.
entries.test: Does a crew view, pip or second camera render on Very Low? If yes it breaks single view.

entries.words: "give the pip views a pleasant border across the game that matches our styleguide."
entries.rule: Every picture-in-picture view wears the one style-guide frame (PipViewFrame: hairline, slivered outline, chrome band).
entries.test: Does the new PiP view own a PipViewFrame rather than a border of its own?

entries.words: Angular. ("Angular is probably good.")
entries.rule: Ability icons are angular, line-weight and monochrome, and may use the hull's own silhouette where it reads (the Dolphin's jaw on its Space icon).
entries.test: Is the icon's drawing angular and built from the hull's real shape where that helps, with no rounded generic glyph?

entries.words: The flower owns the element; an ability icon never repeats its element's mark. ("I don't see what value the redundancy could provide.")
entries.rule: The element flower above the ability row owns the element; an ability icon never repeats its element's mark.
entries.test: Does the icon draw a petal, element glyph or element colour? If yes, remove it: the flower already says it.

entries.words: Elements have no colour (LOCKED, Garrett 2026-10-24). The team colours in §3 never stand for an element: jade is not Time, gold is not Charge, blue is not Mass, ruby is not Space. An element is told by shape and position only.
entries.rule: A domain colour (Jade, Ruby, Gold, Blue) never stands for an element; an element is told by shape and position only.
entries.retired: the lockup's rev 3 element colouring
entries.test: Does the design use a team colour to mean an element, or an element position out of the fixed order? If yes it breaks the rule.

entries.words: "Every pixel is important." Nothing in the UI moves for its own sake while a player is reading or playing.
entries.rule: Nothing in the UI moves for its own sake while a player reads or plays: tab underlines, lattices, orbs, bonds and halos are still; only motion that means something (a spinner, a playing EQ, a teaching hint, a window entrance) is kept.
entries.retired: the sweeping tab underline, the drifting panel lattice, orbiting presence dots, breathing Hangar rings, element halo breathing
entries.test: List every moving thing on the screen: does each one mean something right now? Decoration that moves is cut.

entries.words: Every colour belongs to one of six families, and each family means one thing. A colour that means nothing is Blue.
entries.rule: Every colour in anything Froglet makes belongs to one of six families with one meaning each (Lime call to action, Fire danger, Gold spend, Jade a choice you can change, Ruby no way back, Blue neutral); a colour that means nothing is Blue, and no colour sits in the forbidden band between families.
entries.test: Classify every new colour (colour_domains.py classify): is it inside one family, used for that family's meaning only, and out of the band?

entries.words: Elements carry no colour (LOCKED, Garrett 2026-10-24). Charge, Mass, Space and Time are told by the glyph's shape, by animation and by effects, never by a fixed hue.
entries.rule: Charge, Mass, Space and Time are told by shape, animation and effects, never by a fixed hue; no UI surface, HUD or board colours an element.
entries.retired: the Rev 3 HUD element colours, the ElementRim materials, the Mass/Space/Time button variants, the lockup's elementColour
entries.test: Does any element glyph, bar, card or effect carry a fixed hue that means the element? If yes it breaks the LOCKED rule.

entries.words: "we need to make sure we never conflate the domain colors with elemental identity. jade is not time. gold is not charge. mass is not blue. space is not ruby. and when you do that it confuses players. i know this conflation got introduced recently, but we need to set a rule that we explicitly do not do this."
entries.rule: A domain colour never stands for an element and no element has a colour: an element is told by shape, animation and effects, and a card is tinted by state or by team, never by element.
entries.retired: Rev 3 element colour on the ability cards (approved by Shombith 2026-10-16, retired 2026-10-24)
entries.test: Does any sheet, blob, edge, pip or icon wear a colour that means an element? It fails (check_ui_colors.py).

entries.words: the icons are teaching the ability
entries.rule: An ability icon teaches what the ability does: the real hull in its take (nose to nose for a joust, in its sphere over prisms for a skim), never a generic or borrowed glyph.
entries.retired: the borrowed Sparrow boost icon on the Squirrel, the teal placeholders, the eleven-step ring
entries.test: Could a new player guess the ability from the icon alone, with no caption? If not, it is not teaching.

entries.words: Friends panel should not overlap over any gameplay cards. ... when it is enabled inside the arcade screen the cards move to the right when this panel opens up. It should not move other contents if it is home, hangar or any other screens.
entries.rule: The friends drawer never overlaps a gameplay card: it cannot open over an open game window, on the arcade screen it pushes the cards aside, and on every other screen it slides over without moving content.
entries.test: Open the drawer on each screen: does it cover a card, or shift content anywhere but the arcade grid?

entries.words: The one background motion: the sea lines behind a whole window ... Shombith chose it on 2026-10-25 from the canvas's Rev 12 board ("keep it a bit slow")
entries.rule: The slow sea lines are the only background motion anywhere in the menus (no layer faster than 40 s a loop, never back to one flat colour); the crystal lattice background is gone.
entries.retired: the crystal lattice background (MENU_REDESIGN_B.md section 70)
entries.test: Does a screen add a background motion other than the sea lines, or speed the sea past 40 s a loop? If yes it is out.

entries.words: The card pictures drift (`Docs/MENU_REDESIGN_B.md` §72; Shombith 2026-10-25: "make it have some animation ... for all of the gamemode toy cards"
entries.rule: A game card's art may drift at most 5 x 3 canvas units over 40 s inside its overscan, the cards' one motion and an explicit exception to 'nothing moves for its own sake'; raise it with Garrett if the cards ever read as busy.
entries.test: Does a card animate anything beyond the small slow art drift? If yes it breaks the attention economy.

entries.words: "On PC the gamepad view should only every have the 5 standard ability icons and any additional active controls should be to the left of those (like the squirrel's drift) and it should be labeled with a glyph. this is always true for vessels."
entries.rule: The only controls on a vessel's view are the five standard cards (four elemental and the omni) plus CORE cards to their left, each labelled with its input glyph; a vessel never draws a button of its own over its view.
entries.retired: the Jacks' herding view's zoom and call buttons (rounds 2-9)
entries.test: List every control the vessel's view draws; anything that is not one of the five cards or a CORE card left of them fails.

entries.words: It is too noisy. Keep the preview on the left and the description below. Move the controls to the right side, keep it at the top. Move the intensity and the team and AI selection below it ... Remove the slop below saying dolphin, pilot 2
entries.rule: The configure screen is quiet: preview left with its description below, controls top right, intensity, team and AI below them, one START (no hold-to-launch, no invite button) and no filler text.
entries.retired: the hold-to-launch gesture and the invite-a-friend button on the configure screen
entries.test: Does the configure screen add a second launch gesture, an extra button or decorative text? If yes it is noise.

entries.words: the same card as in Arcade should be there in arena and voyages game configuration card selecting vessel and domain and AI.
entries.rule: One configure card (vessel, domain, AI, intensity) serves Arcade, Arena and Voyage; a mode never gets its own configuration layout.
entries.test: Does the mode's launch screen reuse the one configure card? A bespoke configuration layout is out.

entries.words: you used elemental icon for friends you should never do that.
entries.rule: An element glyph means an element (an ability, a petal, an element bar) and nothing else: never people, a social feature or decoration.
entries.retired: the Space glyph on the friends drawer's title
entries.test: Does any non-element UI wear one of the four element glyphs? If yes replace it with a chrome glyph.

entries.words: Abilities when I click them then only the vessel should perform. Again I say in the hangar we can reduce the size of each component it looks too big in the game
entries.rule: In the Hangar the vessel demonstrates an ability only when its card is clicked and the components stay small; the top strip runs Codex (locked), Hangar, Home, Ark, Port (locked) in that order.
entries.test: Does the Hangar play ability demos unasked, oversize its components or reorder the top strip?

entries.words: I want lavalamp to run infinitely like a screensaver ... without lagging or eating more memory
entries.rule: The menu's lava lamp runs forever like a screensaver without lag or growing memory; a destroyed prism is recycled after its death effect.
entries.test: Does an hour of idle menu grow memory, GameObject count or frame time?

entries.words: during the preview of each game mode when we press fullscreen it goes actual full screen rather the play area should extend as a tray and the other parts of the UI (right side) should get hidden
entries.rule: A mode preview's full screen is a tray that extends the play area and hides the right-side UI, never a true full-screen takeover.
entries.retired: the true full-screen preview
entries.test: Does FULL SCREEN leave the configure window's frame and tray behaviour in place?

entries.words: i didn't mean to move the anchors that was not intentional. the work i liked was the boundary definitions for each region and the forbidden zones.
entries.rule: The colour families' boundaries and the forbidden band are the design; the anchors are the game's own values and are the check, never an input to move.
entries.test: Does a palette change move a family anchor instead of placing a colour inside its region? If yes it is wrong.

entries.words: stop using the rhombuses for shielded prisms, that shape is owned by the time petal ... cut the rhombus in half
entries.rule: The rhombus belongs to the Time petal; a shielded prism in an icon is drawn as two close triangles cut along the long axis.
entries.retired: the whole-rhombus shielded prism in icons
entries.test: Does any icon draw a whole rhombus for something that is not Time?

entries.words: I made a mistake episode 1 is not the hypersea. Episode saga are seperate things and so is quest tracker. SO 4 tabs and Voyage opens up first obviously with episodes coming soon or locked.
entries.rule: The Voyage window has four tabs with Voyage first; the episode saga and the quest tracker are separate tabs, episodes shown coming soon or locked, with the sea lines behind it.
entries.test: Does the Voyage window fold episodes or the quest tracker into the HyperSea voyage, or open on anything but Voyage?

entries.words: use the correct icons for elements, check codex for that ... cards in arcade have these, please fix that too
entries.rule: Element marks everywhere in the menus (control panels, cards) use the Codex's element shapes, never the HUD petal sprite.
entries.test: Does any element mark in the menus draw the HUD petal?

entries.words: The Froglet UI style guide - one look for EVERYTHING Froglet makes
entries.rule: Every surface Froglet makes (game UI, Frogma boards, artifacts and diagrams, decks, the website, the Fleet Codex, every studio) wears the one Froglet style guide and loads its tokens instead of typing colours.
entries.test: Name the style-guide token behind every colour, type size, corner and button state in the design; a hand-typed colour or a second look fails.

entries.words: Garrett's six colour families with one meaning each (Lime is always the call to action; Jade is a choice you can claim and reclaim, the selection and focus; Ruby is no way back, Ready)
entries.rule: Each of the six colour families carries exactly one meaning: Lime is the call to action, Jade is a claimable choice / selection / focus, Ruby is no way back (Ready); a domain is one accent.
entries.test: For every accent on the screen, state its family and check it carries that family's one meaning; the only lime thing is the call to action.

entries.words: remember it will be something that the player unlocks with quest system. So it should something inside the profile view, once done bring up the loading screen like when cell is change that the theme is changing and apply the theme.
entries.rule: Colour sets (themes) are changed from the Profile and are quest unlocks (all unlocked for now); applying one plays the cell-change loading screen.
entries.test: Is the theme picker in the Profile, framed as an unlock, with the loading transition on apply?

entries.words: Ask whether the player can change their mind. A hull they claim in an arena lineup, a friend they add, a tab or tile they select: they can take it back, so it is Jade, and so are the selection and the focus ring. Play and Ready: once pressed there is no way back ... so they are Ruby
entries.rule: Jade marks what the player can claim and reclaim (a pick, the selection, the focus ring); Ruby marks what cannot be taken back (Play, Ready); Lime stays the call to action the player can still change.
entries.retired: the sky-blue selection (#3DB2FF, moving to Jade); lime on focus
entries.test: For each coloured control ask: can the player change their mind? Reclaimable is Jade, irreversible is Ruby, the one thing to do now is Lime.

entries.words: The three domains (Jade, Ruby, Gold) are teams. Only a team thing wears one: your score, your avatar chip, your domain panel.
entries.rule: A domain colour is worn only by a team thing (your score, avatar chip, domain panel); the UI's own Jade, Ruby and Gold tokens mean their uses, never a team.
entries.test: Does a non-team element wear a domain colour, or a team thing wear a UI token? Either confuses the two.

entries.words: CTA is always lime: the important thing the screen asks the player to do that they can still change. Focus and selection are Jade (D3), never lime. Play, which launches a game, is Ruby like Ready
entries.rule: Lime is only the one call to action on a screen; focus and selection are never lime; Play is Ruby like Ready.
entries.test: Does a screen wear lime on anything but its one call to action (a heading, an eyebrow, a selection, decoration)? If yes it is wrong.

entries.words: One component set, two scales: phones (under 600 points tall) get an 800 x 450 canvas and the mobile type column (section 8).
entries.rule: Phones use the same component set at a second scale: an 800 x 450 canvas and the mobile type column, applied by one component on every player-facing canvas, with the phone layout drawn on Frogma first.
entries.test: Is the phone layout drawn and checked at 800 x 450 with the mobile type column, using the same components as desktop?

entries.words: All player-facing text has a human-facing control (LOCKED rule, every branch). Every word the player can read is a serialized field on an SO, prefab or component, or in an authored table.
entries.rule: Every word a player can read is an authored field a human can add, edit, blank or delete without code; computed facts fill tokens in an authored template; an empty field shows nothing, never a hardcoded default.
entries.test: For each string the player sees, name the SO/prefab/table field it lives in; a C# literal reaching a label, toast, dialogue or button fails.

entries.words: The icons run charge → mass → space → time, left to right — the same order as the element flowers above them.
entries.rule: Every vessel HUD shows exactly four ability icons in the lower right, one per ability, in the order Charge, Mass, Space, Time under the element flowers that upgrade them.
entries.test: Does the HUD show four icons in element order under the flowers, with no fifth and no reorder?

entries.words: Every word a player reads is a field a person can edit (CLAUDE.md, LOCKED): a serialized string, or an authored template filled with `TemplateText.Fill`. An empty field shows nothing.
entries.rule: Every word a player can read is an authored field (a serialized string or a template with tokens) a person can edit, blank or delete without code; an empty field shows nothing and never falls back to a hardcoded default.
entries.test: Is any player-facing string a C# literal or a code-built sentence? If yes it must move to an authored field.

entries.words: A toy carries NO TEXT — no name, no label, no progress readout: the ring and the icon do the lift in the world, and the Toy Box menu is where a player learns what a toy is called
entries.rule: In the world a toy shows no text; its switch ring and icon explain it and the Toy Box menu names it (the one exception is SHARE / REPAINT over a finished painting).
entries.test: Does the toy design put any text in the world? A TextMeshPro in a toy fails the gate.

entries.words: There is NO vessel-selection panel, and there must never be another one: changing your hull in freestyle is the Vessel Changer TOY
entries.rule: Changing your hull in freestyle is the Vessel Changer toy (flown, or opened from the Toy Box); there is never another vessel-selection panel.
entries.retired: the scene-authored panel of vessel cards (retired 2026-09-23)
entries.test: Does the design add a screen, list or panel that picks a hull outside the Vessel Changer toy?

entries.words: The Four-Icon Ability Row (LOCKED structure — every vessel HUD) ... The icons run charge → mass → space → time, left to right — the same order as the element flowers above them.
entries.rule: Every vessel HUD shows exactly four elemental ability icons in the lower right, charge → mass → space → time under the flowers that upgrade them, plus the omni card; the upgrade is signalled by an authored sprite swap, an element badge and a scale bump, and a gauge colour is never overloaded with upgrade meaning.
entries.test: Does the HUD show four elemental icons in element order under their flowers, with the upgrade signal in all three layers?

entries.words: the pair first shipped domain-LOCKED — rivals were not carried and saw a sealed shell — and its first playtest sealed the Butterfly against its own pair ... The fail-open rule and `Settings.Owner` that fixed it carry straight over to the toll.
entries.rule: A wormhole mouth fails open: rivals are carried through (and tolled) rather than sealed out; only an unpaired, withering mouth is sealed.
entries.retired: domain-locked sealing of the wormhole pair
entries.test: Can a vessel ever see a sealed shell on a live pair? If yes it has gone domain-locked again.

entries.words: "there should always be a one to one relationship between scored hits and petal theft so immunity from one is the same as the other. knockback and shrink should no longer be an effect that vessels can do to each other. we should only be affecting petals to score points. no other pvp in the game"
entries.rule: The only thing one pilot may do to another is move their petals, and every such move is a scored hit through one gate (a ward against one is a ward against both); no knockback, shrink, spin, slow, stun, input mute or structure laid at a pilot; arena prism effects hit whoever flies in but may never be aimed at a pilot.
entries.retired: knockback on other vessels (VesselImpulseByExplosionEffectSO), VesselShrinkSkimmerEffectSO, the Rhino's VesselDangerBlockFormationBySkimmerEffectSO and its sword's danger dome, the Butterfly dust's decaying debuff
entries.test: List every effect the design has on an opposing vessel; each must be a petal move that scores through CombatHitDrain.TryAdmit, and nothing else.

entries.words: Rhino's absence is a DESIGN statement since 2026-10-16, not a gap — "the bulldozer ignores mass"
entries.rule: The Rhino ploughs prisms aside and ramming costs it no speed; every other hull that takes the prism slow shares one fleet tuning so a prism reads the same whichever hull hits it.
entries.test: Does a hull's prism contact use the shared fleet slow numbers, or is its difference a recorded design statement like the Rhino's?

entries.words: procedural vessel models are terrible even as placeholders
entries.rule: A vessel's hull is a built FBX model (made by /vessel-model with its bones, element morphs and slots), never a C# procedural HullForm surface, not even as a placeholder.
entries.retired: C# `*HullForm` procedural surfaces as vessel models (and the seven from-scratch hulls of 2026-10-17)
entries.test: Does the brief ship a modelled FBX hull with the shipped names and four element morphs? A generated or placeholder mesh fails.

entries.words: building a framework that meets our intentions not mimic halfbaked examples
entries.rule: The fleet convention is the intention; a quirk in a shipped vessel is a legacy binding with a migration step, never a rule to copy.
entries.test: Does the design copy a shipped vessel's quirk because it ships? Check the fleet convention first.

entries.words: Garrett: control theft is not an economy form — a danger prism BURNS petals and nothing takes controls
entries.rule: Nothing in the game takes a player's controls; a danger prism burns petals.
entries.retired: SparrowDebuffByRhinoDangerPrismEffectSO's 5 s Button2 mute and its event asset (deleted 2026-10-17)
entries.test: Does any effect in the design mute, lock or steal an input? It fails.

entries.words: learn what you can from [the Wrasse and Grouper] ... unify what you can so we have a consistent notion of multiplayer vessels. and apply it here.
entries.rule: Every crew vessel shares one notion: a seat on the hull (ICrewSeat), one card naming both, the shared seat rules, the shared two-view layout and seat camera, and the Vessel Changer as the way in.
entries.test: Does the new crew vessel reuse CrewSeat, CrewPictureInPicture and CrewViewRender, or roll its own seats and views?

entries.words: Each hue family has a name and one meaning. Saturation and value inside a family are free, to tell things apart within the same use.
entries.rule: A vessel wears four things: a domain accent in the pilot's team colour, a neutral Blue body, neutral glass told from the body by saturation and value, and subtle Fire at its jet exits; Lime never appears on a hull.
entries.test: Does the hull's colour scheme add a family beyond domain, Blue and Fire, or put Lime (the call to action) on the vessel?

entries.words: The look: a spaceship inspired by a meerkat, never the animal (Garrett, 2026-10-18), and not the Stoat recoloured.
entries.rule: A vessel is a spaceship inspired by its animal, never the animal, and never another hull recoloured.
entries.test: Does the hull read as a creature with a face and limbs, or as a ship whose silhouette says its animal?

entries.words: Let's have all charge based abilities that strip/steal elements also silence charge and space attacks for a duration proportional to the elements stripped/stolen. ... Mass and time abilities should remain untouched, so players remain fully maneuverable and can still cultivate new mass.
entries.rule: Every scored hit that takes a rival's petals also silences them for what the hit is worth (one second a petal, capped at 8 s): their Charge and Space attacks cannot harm while silenced, while their Mass and Time abilities and all manoeuvring stay untouched.
entries.test: Does the design add a way to take petals without silencing by worth, or silence anything beyond harm (movement, Mass, Time)? Either breaks the fleet-wide silence rule.

entries.words: Danger prisms are never silenced but the ability to produce them might be. ... We want vessels to still use their abilities, but those abilities can not harm vessels, fauna, or prisms while silenced.
entries.rule: Silence removes only harm: every ability still fires and every control answers, but nothing a silenced pilot does can harm vessels, fauna or prisms, a prism they lay comes out plain, and danger prisms already standing keep their danger.
entries.test: Does the silenced state block an input, stop an ability from playing, or leave any of its harm live? Any of those is wrong.

entries.words: Asked to choose between a starting stake in the combat modes, silencing every scored hit by its worth, or leaving it, Garrett chose silence every scored hit.
entries.rule: Silence is bought by a hit's worth in petals at the fleet price, not by the petals that actually came loose, so a fresh pilot with an empty pot is silenced like a full one.
entries.retired: silencing for settled petals only (the first cut)
entries.test: Would a scored hit on a pilot holding no petals silence them for the hit's worth? If not, the design has gone back to petals settled.

entries.words: Silence (Garrett, 2026-10-20) is the one consequence a scored hit carries beyond the petals.
entries.rule: A scored hit silences its victim for what it is worth (1 s per petal, capped at 8 s): every ability still works but harms nothing and lays no danger; no motion or control is taken; a silenced attacker neither scores nor takes.
entries.test: Does the hit's consequence ride the scored hit itself and take only harmlessness, never motion or control?

entries.words: A hovering assembly (`/vessel-model` section 0.5, Garrett 2026-10-21): the beak, turret, wings and tail fan each float clear of the hull
entries.rule: A hull is a hovering assembly: its beak, turret, wings and fans float clear of the hull (about 1-2% of the diagonal), nothing welded on.
entries.retired: the seven from-scratch hulls of 2026-10-17 (retired 2026-10-18)
entries.test: Does every part of the model float clear of the hull (assembly_report.py)? A welded part is out.

entries.words: Invert Y / Invert Throttle are the settings' alone (2026-10-21).
entries.rule: Inversion is applied once by the player's settings at the end of every input mix; no strategy or hull carries a pitch sign of its own (a hull's touch tilt flip is hull data under the same rule).
entries.test: Does any input strategy or hull in the design flip an axis on its own? It fails (InputInversionTests).

entries.words: A human pilot's nose has no lag (2026-10-21).
entries.rule: The local human pilot's nose follows the commanded rotation each frame on every device; AI, autopilot and remote hulls keep the fleet's 1.5/s lag, which only a mode may set per AI.
entries.test: Does the design add nose lag to a human pilot's input? It fails; the Garrett 2026-10-23 per-device dial is the only lag a human flies.

entries.words: both thumbs off should read as both triggers pulled and switch to gyro controls
entries.rule: On a phone each hull has its own touch profile (thumb lifts or totem buttons, tilt, extra buttons); a tilt flip is hull data under the one Invert Y rule, and both thumbs off reads as both triggers pulled and switches to gyro (tilt) controls.
entries.test: With no thumb on the glass, do both triggers read fully pulled and does tilt steer? Is any axis flip authored as hull data rather than in a strategy?

entries.words: The nose lag is one dial per device, never per hull (Garrett, 2026-10-23). ... ("responsive, but eases into its target ... we want to keep this on gamepad")
entries.rule: A human pilot's nose lag is one dial per device (gamepad 1.5/s, touch 9/s, keyboard and mouse none), never per hull; no response curve and no multi-stage smoothing on the stick.
entries.retired: a response curve on stick position and a 4-6 stage smoothing chain (flown and rejected on the pad)
entries.test: Does any hull author its own nose lag or stick curve? It fails; only the device's dial applies.

entries.words: a new vessel is prototyped in the artifact WITH its mini-game and its four abilities (the element map, the level-5 upgrades)
entries.rule: A new vessel is designed as one package: the hull, its own mini-game and its four elemental abilities with their level-5 upgrades; all three reach the game together (hull to the Vessel Changer, mini-game as a real mode, abilities as the element map).
entries.retired: the 2026-10-14 "three surfaces" rule
entries.test: Does the vessel brief name its mini-game and all four abilities with their L5 upgrades? A hull alone is incomplete.

entries.words: a pilot grants a vision power. Hold the left bumper and the one thing your pilot sees (one of eighteen callsigns built from the fundamentals) lights up while everything else is suppressed. A pilot no longer swaps any part of a vessel's kit
entries.rule: A pilot grants a vision power (hold LB: the one thing the callsign sees lights up, everything else is suppressed) and never swaps any part of a vessel's kit.
entries.retired: the pilot as a kit side-grade (PILOTS_AND_ARTIFACTS.md sections 0, 2, 4 and 6)
entries.test: Does the pilot design change an ability, a number or a control on the vessel? If yes it is a kit change, not a pilot.

entries.words: an artifact transforms the payload, a parcel of the Ark's hull that any vessel grabs and fires to crack super-shielded mass. An artifact no longer turns a "fifth knob"
entries.rule: An artifact transforms the Ark payload any vessel grabs and fires to crack super-shielded mass; it never turns a fifth knob on the vessel itself.
entries.retired: the artifact as a fifth knob (PILOTS_AND_ARTIFACTS.md section 3)
entries.test: Does the artifact design tune the vessel rather than transform the payload? If yes it is a kit change.

entries.words: it should feel big ... like its own level ... a kaiju protected by three vessels and its own regeneration
entries.rule: The Ark feels big, like its own level: a kaiju protected by three escorts and its own regeneration, with engines that animate, octahedral shielded prisms placed to protect the rest, danger prisms where it wants to be dangerous, and a hangar the escorts launch from.
entries.test: Does the Ark design read as a level-sized kaiju with escorts, regeneration and a hangar, not merely a big vessel?

entries.words: Think hierarchical and heterarchical. Look at the dolphin and the details of its contours ... this ark should have 5 hierarchies that have 2 to 5 heterarchies each. It should look sophisticated like it belongs on the cover of a sci fi novel, not like megaknight turned into a toy spaceship.
entries.rule: A hull's form language is hierarchical and heterarchical (five levels of form, each with two to five sibling forms): crisp faceted masses, secondary forms, surface systems, then micro detail, sophisticated like a sci-fi novel cover, never a bubbly toy.
entries.test: Count the levels of form on the model: are there five, each carrying two to five heterarchies, down to micro detail?

entries.words: Nothing is round for its own sake, nothing is a spike, and nothing stands on a pedestal.
entries.rule: On a hull nothing is round for its own sake, nothing is a spike, and nothing stands on a pedestal.
entries.test: Does the model carry a dome, spike or plinth that serves no form? Remove it.

entries.words: "the meerkat should be producing a new fundamental (solitons)"
entries.rule: A soliton is a standing tunnel through space that keeps its shape, carries whatever enters one mouth out of the other, and is seen only by the way it bends the world (no grid, no surface); anyone may ride one, what it fires is a moving prism scored to its maker, and it never deletes mass.
entries.test: Does the tunnel design keep its shape, carry riders and prisms through, conserve mass and show itself only as bent space?

entries.words: lock in the elemental definition so yash builds upon them.
entries.rule: The Meerkat's element definition is locked: Space the Soliton (surface area by level, L5 Steal), Time faster through every soliton (L5 Boost Out), Charge Sentinel mode (L5 Six Sentinels), Mass the Exit Portal (L5 Danger Portal); how each is built stays Yash's.
entries.retired: Yash's round-8 proposals (Lookout, Hardened Bridge, Cave-in, Chain Dig) and the round-18 Mix's L5 swaps
entries.test: Does a Meerkat change move an ability to another element or alter a row's meaning? If yes it reopens a locked definition.

entries.words: The omni crystal is always one size (Garrett, 2026-10-28). Nothing resizes it: not the reactor, and not the Charge shape
entries.rule: The omni crystal is always one size; no reactor, element shape or effect resizes it.
entries.test: Does anything scale the omni crystal? If yes it is wrong.

entries.words: the rest is design, Docs/Studios/MEERKAT.md § Garrett's direction, whose element definition is LOCKED (Garrett, 2026-10-28)
entries.rule: The Meerkat soliton's element definition (what each of its elements does, per Garrett's direction in MEERKAT.md) is fixed; a design may extend the soliton but not redefine its elements.
entries.test: Check each element's role in the brief against MEERKAT.md § Garrett's direction; any change needs Garrett.

entries.words: Yash's call: rival vessels CAN choose to ride your Skimshell — opt-in by the rival, e.g. entering flat and holding their own input — and it must never forcibly move an opposing vessel against its will.
entries.rule: (Proposed by Yash, flagged for Garrett, not yet reviewed) a rival may opt in to ride a Stoat's Skimshell by their own input, but the shell must never move an opposing vessel against its will.
entries.test: Does a field, shell or pull move a rival who did not choose to enter it? If yes it breaks section 9; an opt-in ride must be the rival's own input.

entries.words: there is an unfun state where the best paths are no longer crossable ...
entries.rule: A destroyed stretch of the Goby's trail is a real gap the Pistol must clear; a fall never hits phantom prisms and never leaves the best path uncrossable: it restores the gap it touched and sets the Pistol down beyond it.
entries.retired: the vortex-ring ride back to the den after a fall (the 2026-10-28 design)
entries.test: Can the Pistol ever be stuck with no crossable path, or land on prisms that are not there?

entries.words: For now we won't be making any more new vessels. We will be focusing on making the mini games. The time mini games, all our existing vessels, awesome. And then finally we will make arena games such as regattas.
entries.rule: No new vessels: the work is each existing vessel's Time minigame first, then the arena games; every vessel prototype is parked and catalogued, and one is brought back only when an owner asks.
entries.retired: the ten concept vessels, the Siphonophore, the Omega crews, the calm three and the Orca's play styles (parked, CONCEPT_FLEET.md section 13)
entries.test: Does the design add a new hull? If yes it is parked until an owner asks; make an existing vessel's Time game better instead.

entries.words: I think we keep only the orbit effect of stoat, and remove the pathfinding field trajectory effect
entries.rule: The Stoat's kit is the orbit alone; the pathfinding field trajectory is parked.
entries.retired: the Stoat's field trajectory (STOAT_FIELD_TRAJECTORY_PARKED.md)
entries.test: Does a Stoat design rest on the field trajectory? If yes it builds on a parked feature.

entries.words: the sparrow knocks other vessels around. this is not fun to receive. vessels should not be able to move opponent vessels.
entries.rule: An offensive act against another pilot may take their elemental crystals and nothing else: no vessel may move an opposing vessel (a shove, a spin, a pull it did not choose) or take its controls (a muted stick, a shrunk skimmer, a frozen trail); referred to as LOCKED by BLACK_HOLE.md and SILENCE.md.
entries.retired: the Sparrow's knockback; the danger-prism control mute (2026-10-17)
entries.test: Does the design displace, re-aim or restrain a rival vessel, or mute any of its inputs? If yes it is out; take petals instead.

entries.words: Vessels — the player/AI actors whose class-specific abilities compose with the fundamentals above.
entries.rule: A vessel's class abilities compose with the fundamentals (mass, domain, elementals, prisms, cells, flora & fauna) rather than adding systems beside them.
entries.test: For each ability, name the fundamentals it reaches; an ability that needs a system of its own fails.

entries.words: A pilot does not interact with their own trail while they are MAKING it
entries.rule: A vessel and its skimmer ignore the trail they are laying, so a drift, Mass scaling or a large skimmer cannot feed on or ram the pilot's own fresh ribbon.
entries.test: Can the hull or skimmer in the design touch its own trail prisms while laying them?

entries.words: MASS in-flight growth is a HIT VOLUME, not a size. ... ONE ROUND IS ONE STROKE; THE VOLLEY IS THE SPHERE.
entries.rule: A projectile's model keeps its muzzle size for its whole flight; Mass growth is shown as a see-through shell sized to the swept hit radius; one round draws a single bolt and the volley makes the sphere, never a crackling ball per round.
entries.retired: swelling the round's model with Mass (a small ship firing cannonballs)
entries.test: Does Mass scale the round's mesh, or only the shell that is the hit volume?

entries.words: The vessel's own hull conveys its element levels: vessel models carry blend shapes on their skinned meshes labeled by element name
entries.rule: A vessel's model is an element display: labelled shape keys morph the hull through the [0, 10] band as its levels move, and transitions glide, never snap.
entries.test: Does the hull ship element-labelled shape keys that move it, and does the morph glide?

entries.words: The crackle is meant to be a vessel's ONLY skim visual
entries.rule: A skim is shown by the forcefield crackle on the skimmer sphere and nothing else; no container holds the legacy beam.
entries.retired: the legacy skim beam (SkimmerFXPrismEffectSO; the Squirrel's beam retired 2026-10-06, owner's call)
entries.test: Does the vessel's skim container draw anything but the crackle?

entries.words: Nothing in the world looks flat (LOCKED, Garrett 2026-10-18) ... "Nothing in the environment should ever look flat like this, that is reserved for ui."
entries.rule: Anything drawn in the world (an effect, wave, marker, trail, blast) is a lit, faceted volume whose thicknesses scale with its own size, never a flat sheet, unlit fill, additive ribbon or billboard; flat is the UI's look; an owner's explicit call for one view wins and is recorded where it is made.
entries.retired: the ring explosion, the spindle facets and the black hole's vortex ring drawn flat (each redrawn)
entries.test: Would a test that flattens the effect fail (most facets face sideways, it stands out of its plane), and are its thicknesses a share of its size?

entries.words: dynamic clipping should never do nothing
entries.rule: A moving thing that passes through a prism always acknowledges the contact even when nothing happens mechanically (own armoured mass lights up, super-shielded rival mass jiggles); a contact that does nothing reads as a clip.
entries.test: Is there any contact between a moving effect and a prism that leaves no visible answer? If yes, light or jiggle it.

entries.words: the main driver is performance... smooth is the requirement... improving their look from afar is the nice-to-have
entries.rule: A spindle LOD is judged by performance first and a seamless transition second; a better far look is the stretch, never the reason.
entries.test: Does the LOD change cost frames or show a visible switch? Either fails before any look gain counts.

entries.words: instead of a 2d effect we just have a client side perimeter of 3d craziness on the perimeter where vignettes typically use 2d effects
entries.rule: A screen-edge state effect is a 3D perimeter of faceted volumes refracting the frame, drawn on the local pilot's camera only, never a flat 2D vignette.
entries.retired: the 2D danger vignette
entries.test: Is any full-screen or edge state effect a flat 2D overlay? If yes, redraw it as a lit, faceted 3D perimeter.

entries.words: Cytoplasm shards are thinned, never removed. They point at the cell's crystal (Garrett, 2026-10-21)
entries.rule: Cytoplasm shards are a navigation cue pointing at the cell's crystal: a quality tier thins them (never under a tenth) and never removes them.
entries.retired: the disableCytoplasm flag
entries.test: Does any tier, preset or mode remove the cytoplasm or thin it under the floor?

entries.words: Let's also apply this to all spindles including fauna like sharks. Let's also replace the switch rings with a spindle material that has this effect.
entries.rule: Every spindle wearer, fauna and rings included, carries the one spindle LOD and depth effect; no model draws its own version.
entries.test: Does a new creature or construct draw spindles without the shared LOD and depth effect?

entries.words: Make a synthetic spindle geometry that is more like a wire instead of a root. Use this for the switch rings in a similar LOD fashion, so these look like synthetic constructs up close, but spindles from afar.
entries.rule: A made thing (a switch ring) is a synthetic machined wire up close and reads as a spindle from afar; grown things keep the root braid.
entries.test: Is the construct's near geometry a wire and its far tiers the shared spindle thread?

entries.words: increase the fidelity on the fly by wire missiles. they feel cheap. the bomb should not have a ring that says burst. it should use a lit state to show what it will destroy.
entries.rule: A blast's reach is shown by lighting what it will destroy in the world, never by a ring; projectiles carry enough fidelity not to feel cheap.
entries.retired: the bomb's burst ring
entries.test: Does the effect draw a ring or marker to say its reach instead of lighting the prisms it will take?

entries.words: In the world, not on the screen (LOCKED, Garrett 2026-10-21) ... "always go for the 3d in world solution over the 2d flat text solution."
entries.rule: A fact about the world (what a blast will catch, where a shot lands, what is targeted, a thing's state) is shown on the thing itself in 3D (lit, coloured, shaped, moved), never as a screen ring, label or word; the crosshair stays a small aim mark.
entries.retired: the Orca bomb seat's blast-size ring and "BURST" label (round 9)
entries.test: For every world fact the player must read, is it on the thing in 3D through PrismLit, morphs, petals or a lit volume rather than 2D text or a ring?

entries.words: make the vortex ring loose the flat effect and replace it with a cool warping effect like the black holes use but convey a more subtle toroid instead of a spherical singularity
entries.rule: The Pistol's vortex ring is a subtle lensed toroid (bent light round its core circle, a faint rim), never a flat ring.
entries.retired: the flat vortex ring
entries.test: Does the ring read as a flat disc on screen from any angle? If yes it breaks nothing-flat.

entries.words: Right now mass crystals and omnicrystals are the hardest to distinguish. Shift the colors on each element to match the color shifts we used for the wrasse's 2d elements.
entries.rule: Each free elemental crystal wears its own element's lime shade (the Wrasse's four), so Mass and omni never look alike.
entries.test: Can the four free crystals and the omni be told apart at a glance by their lime shades?

entries.words: When the elemental crystals combine have them retain their separate colors. Change the omnicrystal to retain all four elemental colors of lime in all instances.
entries.rule: An element's shapes wear that element's shade wherever they are: combining crystals keep their colours, and the omni crystal wears all four shades, each on its element's shapes, in every instance.
entries.retired: the one-lime omni and the converter's ease to one lime
entries.test: Does any crystal, converter or omni effect blend the element shades into one lime? If yes it breaks the rule.

entries.words: make sure we are not warping space, we need to make the shaders mobile friendly ... I want to do the same with these black / white hole pair, It should be mobile frames performant and also a subtle clean refreshing user experience.
entries.rule: The black and white hole pair ships the Mobile look: no space warp, mobile-performant, subtle and clean; the full lens stays only for the studio and A/B.
entries.retired: the lens look as the shipped default (StudioLens kept behind BlackHoleConfig.look)
entries.test: Does the hole effect warp the frame or cost a phone its frame rate? If yes it is the studio look, not the shipped one.

entries.words: just keep one high quality look, the one there is now, then document other shaders, so we can recreate later if needed, delete the shaders.
entries.rule: One wormhole shader and one look ship; every other look is documented step by step and deleted, never kept as a preset.
entries.retired: every other wormhole/tunnel shader, material, view and lab button
entries.test: Does the design add a second tunnel look or keep an old one as a switch? If yes, document it and delete it.

entries.words: I dont want any water shader, or underwater look, I want to feel Im inside the wormhole, but the distortion of space time should be configurable, so that users travelling inside the warmhole won't feel dizzy or puke.
entries.rule: A wormhole tunnel feels like being inside a wormhole, with no water or underwater look, and its space-time distortion is configurable and calm so nobody gets dizzy.
entries.retired: the watery pipe (section 5a), the aquarium tube (5b), the per-person look presets
entries.test: Does the tunnel read as water or glass, or distort so hard it could make a rider sick? Either is out.

entries.words: pleasant calm distortion, little jelly like clear liquidy hollow from inside tree trunk, same will be for the root. The trunk and the root of the wormhole tree will be same look, same parameters just for separate trunk / root look.
entries.rule: Trunk and root of the wormhole tree share one look, a clear calm jelly hollow, with the same parameters and only a trunk/root switch.
entries.test: Do trunk and root use one shader and one parameter set? A second look for the root is out.

entries.words: cyan = jade which is a domain color. use Lime for shield. a lit domain color for grow and restore. I did not see any restores. it seemed like that did not work. lets get the juice on landing instead of as its happening
entries.rule: Shield feedback is Lime, grow and restore are a lit domain colour (never cyan, which is Jade), and the juice plays on landing, not while it happens.
entries.test: Does any effect use a domain hue for a non-domain meaning, or play its reward before the moment lands?

entries.words: keep them similar hues so they don't have the ugly multitone interactions when grouped. ... so we might get more ability to distinguish them quickly, especially the wrasse, if they are different lightnesses ... make charge the darkest because its plasma lights it up.
entries.rule: The four element shades are one lime hue at four evenly spaced lightnesses, Charge darkest to Time lightest, so grouped elements never clash and are told apart by lightness.
entries.retired: the four hue-varied lime shades of 2026-10-21 (COLOR.md section 5b)
entries.test: Are the element shades one hue differing only in lightness, in the order Charge, Mass, Space, Time, all inside Lime?

entries.words: The law that makes it teachable is one line: THE RING IS THE TRIGGER VOLUME, DRAWN AT ITS OWN RADIUS
entries.rule: A switch ring is drawn at the radius of its own trigger volume; a ring drawn smaller than its trigger is legal, a ring drawn larger is a lie.
entries.test: Compare the drawn ring radius with the trigger collider radius; drawn larger fails.

entries.words: A switch wearing a playable DOMAIN's colour is reserved: it is one that HANDS you that domain
entries.rule: A switch painted in a playable domain's colour hands you that domain; every other switch is Neutral (Domains.Blue), and the signal, never the caller, picks the colour.
entries.test: Does any ring wear a playable domain's colour without granting that domain? Then it fails.

entries.words: The cone is no longer part of this vocabulary — as a BODY (one you fly at, rather than a hub inside a ring) it is reserved for a booster
entries.rule: A cone body you fly at means booster and nothing else; a toy's meaning sits in its switch ring's shader, not in a cone shape.
entries.retired: the Domain Changer's cone body (became a switch)
entries.test: Does the design use a cone body for anything but a booster?

entries.words: Lit — mass standing inside a force volume is LIT, in the colour of whoever owns that force.
entries.rule: Mass about to be acted on by a force is lit in its owner's colour (a pending blast, an armed warhead, a spared passthrough); a light stores nothing on the prism, decides no outcome, and may be restricted to one domain's mass only when its sentence is about mass its owner owns.
entries.retired: the own-domain explosion's 2-second temporary shield (replaced by the passthrough light)
entries.test: Does the design say "this mass is about to be acted on" through PrismLit rather than a shield, ring or label, and does nothing read the light to decide a kill?

entries.words: So adding a producer is two questions, not one — who is this sentence for, and is it on all the time.
entries.rule: A new light producer must be addressed to a rival (something they need to read) and must not be always on; an always-on light evicts every light that carries information.
entries.retired: the always-on skim field light (built as a fourth producer and cut on a look call after playtest)
entries.test: Who is the light's sentence for, and is it on all the time? A light for its own pilot or an always-on light fails.

entries.words: Continuity of existence — nothing pops in or out (PLATFORM-WIDE LAW, all of Cosmic Shore). Nothing may instantly appear or disappear. Every entity — prisms, crystals, flora, fauna, vessels, projectiles, even UI — must grow / bloom / fade / suction / wither / evaporate into and out of existence over a visible transition.
entries.rule: Nothing the player can see appears or disappears instantly, UI included: spawns bloom or grow in, deaths wither from the extremities inward, suction or fade out.
entries.test: For every spawn and removal in the design, name its visible transition; a bare instantiate-then-show or destroy fails.

entries.words: a vessel's trail, an authored environment and the SKELETON a dead lifeform leaves behind (HealthPrism.LeaveAsSkeleton clears the stamp) all stay still, so a player can tell a plant that is alive from the husk of one that is not without being told.
entries.rule: Living mass moves with its limb's sway; trails, authored environment and a dead lifeform's skeleton stay still, so alive and dead read without a label.
entries.test: Does the living thing visibly move and the husk stay still, with no text telling the player which is which?

entries.words: A cell composed for a CAMERA is budgeted differently from one composed for a PILOT — and the difference is one rule: spend prisms on LENGTH and SILHOUETTE, never on surface.
entries.rule: A world seen from a distant camera (the home screen) spends its prisms on length and silhouette with depth replacing detail, never on surface; a world flown inside is budgeted for the pilot.
entries.test: At the camera's real range, does each prism read as silhouette or is it wasted surface?

entries.words: A species' shape may be a FUNCTION, and then the plant's job is only to DISCOVER it — as a cage of curves, never as a skin.
entries.rule: A plant whose shape is a function traces it as an open cage of curves the player sees through, never as a solid skin.
entries.test: Is the function-shaped plant dense along curves and sparse across them, with the surface visible through it?

entries.words: Every vessel is progressively re-shaded into a flat, cel-banded silhouette in its own DOMAIN colour as a function of its distance from the camera drawing it — the aid that lets pilots find each other at arena range. Not a feature a vessel, scene or mode may choose.
entries.rule: Every vessel fades into a cel-banded silhouette in its own domain colour by distance, with graded edges so the mark never pops, and the local pilot's own vessel excluded; no vessel, scene or mode opts out.
entries.test: Does the new hull or view keep the vision band, exclude the local pilot, and leave the graded edges alone?

entries.words: Your own cone is untouched and wins outright on every prism it covers ... "whose is this" is the one question the platform always answers with domain colour
entries.rule: A pilot's own aim light is never recoloured, brightened or dimmed by a rival's; peers mark only mass your own sight is not marking and blend among themselves by domain hue desaturated toward white, never summed.
entries.test: Can another pilot's instrument change what your own aim shows, and is "whose" told by domain hue?
